block: Block 1: D2 escalation-viable x W2 slow world

games.name: Arms Race Unbound
games.seed: Both sides open with maximum-capability postures and no coordination mechanisms. Blue systems race to deploy denial-prediction, documentation, and auto-appeal AI; Red deploys autonomous payment-integrity and prior-auth automation at frontier pace. No detente offers on the table at start. Green is dissatisfied with trend but has not yet organized. Vendor duopoly is selling hard to both sides.

turns.narrative:
Turn 1 closed the way W2 environments usually do: loudly at the negotiating table, quietly everywhere else. The defining collision was at RegionalMutual's renewal desk, where Lakeview and Prairie arrived with process asks at the exact moment RegionalMutual arrived with its squeeze. Leverage decided it. Prairie signed the tightened documentation standards and expanded prepay categories as drafted; Lakeview traded — it got the gold-card enrollment, a co-announced CMS-0057-F API partnership, and diluted quarterly denial reporting, but ate shortened filing windows and lost its deemed-approval SLA and tolling asks. Meanwhile RegionalMutual quietly licensed NationalCo's PI stack rather than fund the Vendor duopoly — capability that won't be production until 2028, but it raises Red's coalition CD floor.

On the ASO book, the arms race was not a wash. NationalCo's post-pay audit escalation ran into a Blue defense still at a 14% claims-AI deployment base: a CD gap of roughly five on audit surfaces, 60-80% swing capture, booked as fee revenue with no MLR drag. Blue's appeal counteroffensive was real but thin in year one — Meridian's Vendor bridge shrank to a point-solution feed after the duopoly declined the anchor engagement and poached from its build team — so Blue's appeals push mostly held overturn rates flat against the base-rate decline rather than clawing the swing back.

The strategic surprise was Green's speed. The Purchaser Claims-Integrity Coalition formed inside the window Vendor's PlanGuard pitch assumed was open; the coalition mandated a conflict-free auditor and its ownership-mapping exhibit now documents Crucible's both-sides structure as a discoverable fact. Red's retention shield still worked where W2 says it should — the unorganized employer majority signed transparency-for-extension addenda pushing renewals past 2029 — but the dozen organized jumbos forced hybrids with prospective clawback of fees on overturned recoveries.

The environment stayed asleep. CMS greeted its own January 2027 API deadline with enforcement-discretion guidance for good-faith implementers, stranding Summit's genuine first-mover build with exactly one production counterparty (GovProgramCo, whose compliance-forward sequencing was the cleanest Red move of the turn). One state passed a physician-review AI-UM statute that bites no earlier than 2028 and never touches the self-funded book. One business-press story on the dual-sided vendor flared and died. Patient appeal bots grew from roughly 2% to 4% of contested determinations — niche, but Green's clawback math and Prairie's routing both feed on it.

Score the turn honestly: Red banked durable yield, Blue paid formation costs for T2 capability, Green built the record, Vendor grew while its exit thesis acquired a paper trail.
env: CMS (scheduled + W2 posture): The January 2027 CMS-0057-F compliance date arrived accompanied by enforcement-discretion guidance — plans demonstrating good-faith implementation may attest; corrective action deferred. Trade press covered it; general media did not. Effect: payer API readiness stays patchy, Summit's first-mover value defers to 2028+, GovProgramCo's early build becomes an optics asset.

Regulatory (the turn's 1-in-3 roll, hit): One state enacted a physician-review AI-UM statute (SB1120-class). Rulemaking deferred, enforcement budget thin, no reach into self-funded plans (ERISA §514). First audits projected 2028+. Symbolic this turn.

Media (1-in-2 roll, hit; single-turn flare): A business-press investigative piece — sourced substantially from Green's forensic white paper — profiled the PE-backed vendor earning fees on both the generation and the defense of the same denials. No national pickup, no follow-on cycle; story decayed by turn end. The documentary exhibit, unlike the coverage, persists.

Courts (1-in-4 roll, miss — background only): No new consequential ruling. Existing algorithmic-denial dockets (Lokken-class) ground forward in discovery per the litigation clock; one unrelated AI-denial class settled quietly, cash-only, terms sealed, no process commitments — the W2 signature outcome.

State AG: One AG opened an informal inquiry into dual-sided PI/appeals vendor arrangements following Green's routed referral. W2 base rate: reactive posture, likely closes without action absent a fresh shock. Logged as tinder, not fire.

Patient-side appeal AI (exogenous): Contested-determination share assisted by consumer tools grew from ~2% to ~4%, concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members. Prairie's routing program is locally material and nationally invisible. Overturn outcomes from this channel feed Green's clawback arithmetic.

Labor market: Persistent scarcity of experienced SIU, coding, and A/R talent (per evidence brief) made Vendor's raids effective — 2-3 senior SIU departures from NationalCo/GovProgramCo, and measurable slippage on Meridian's build team. Modest wage inflation in exception-management roles on both sides; symmetric admin-cost drag recorded in each side's own ledger per 3.5 as modified by D2 (paid, not canceled).

sign.instrument: Lakeview-RegionalMutual Renewal Rider
sign.detail: Pure process currency — gold-carding criteria (checklist item 9), escalation SLAs, transparency reporting (items 6-7), tolling, API partnership. No corridors or quotas. Signability is not signature: RegionalMutual signed items 1, 3 (diluted), and 5; refused deemed-approval SLA breach and tolling at the bargaining table. As-signed subset recorded.

sign.detail: Checklist item 4 (pooled denial observatory): convertible only. White strikes the current-period pooled training-data feed and converts to independent-TPA-managed, aggregated, de-identified outputs lagged 3+ months, no participant access to rivals' disaggregated data, no rate/price/contract-term data ever. Contribution-gated access teeth survive. Conversion degrades but does not destroy the D2 capability-leapfrog value; evidentiary-record function (unilateral document retention) unaffected.

sign.detail: Ordinary commercial contingency contract with audit rights and escrow (item 8 analog). Vendor signed only a narrowed conflict-disclosure covenant ('materially adverse concurrent engagements' defined tightly) and confined the Meridian engagement to a point-solution content feed per its own go-to-market. Covenant breach remains a discoverable fact.

sign.instrument: Red ASO Transparency & Term-Extension Addendum
sign.detail: Disclosure, data-access, and scoped-audit terms — all process form; term extension is ordinary commercial consideration. Signed broadly by non-coalition employers; coalition accounts forced hybrid riders adding prospective clawback of fees on overturned recoveries.

sign.instrument: RegionalMutual Selective Gold-Card Program
sign.detail: Published objective criteria modeled on Tex. Ins. Code ch. 4201 subch. N (item 9). Signable as-is; White notes on the record that the 95% threshold on low-variance codes concedes near-zero volume, consistent with the ~3% statutory uptake base rate — cover, not concession.

sign.instrument: Green ASO Model Terms v1
sign.detail: Data access, audit rights, fee transparency, conflict disclosure, member-denial SLAs — process terms throughout; the overturn-triggered fee clawback is a commercial fee term, not a denial quota, and passes. Two White notes: 'unrestricted' audit rights read down to scoped-with-chosen-auditor (item 8 symmetry norm); coalition members must negotiate fee terms account-by-account to stay clear of buyer-side coordination exposure post-2023 safety-zone withdrawal — Green's counsel had already structured this.

sign.instrument: Green Direct-Contract Episode Agreement (pilot)
sign.detail: Prospective bundles, contractual gold-carding replacing PA, independent TPA — all signable; ERISA plans contracting directly are squarely within their rights. Pilot scope honored; scale claims would be struck under 3.2 but none were made.

signposts: T2 hinge #1 — RegionalMutual's white-label PI stack reaches production in 2028: expect denial/audit intensity on Lakeview and Prairie to press the +2pt bounded-movement ceiling; Lakeview's only new shields are the signed rider subset and coalition appeal rails.

T2 hinge #2 — Blue cooperative's first lagged data release (2027H2) triggers the D2 CD recompute test: if payer-behavior aggregates measurably lift Blue's model quality, Red's 60-80% swing capture on audit surfaces narrows prospectively.

T2 hinge #3 — The 2027-28 ASO renewal wave is where Green's Model Terms either bind broadly or die: watch whether Red's extension shield holds the stranded accounts and whether the Summit direct-contract pilot posts credible episode economics in time to arm Green's negotiators.

Cumulative litigation/regulatory shock probability stands at ~5-10% after one turn; Green's ownership-mapping exhibit and demand-letter refusal log are pre-positioned accelerants if any shock rolls — but W2 physics mean nothing lands before 2029.

GovProgramCo's dormant MA-tightening ramp keys to the 2027 measurement year: if CMS holds the Stars overhaul schedule, expect MA prior-auth aggression to rise in T2-T3 exactly as the complaints/appeals penalty structure sunsets.

Vendor's conflict-exposure flag is at maximum: Payer Playbook / Provider Signal telemetry pooling is now operational fact, Green holds the corporate map, and one AG inquiry is open. In W2 this stays dormant; any world-model surprise converts it to a solvency-of-thesis event before the 2030 exit.

Meridian's board decides L2 appeal autonomy in late 2028 after the accuracy audit — the single largest swing factor in whether Blue's appeal-coverage attack on the 40% non-appeal gap reaches scale before game end.
Patient-AI trajectory check: W2 caps the channel at 8-10% by 2030; if observed growth exceeds ~2x per turn, players should suspect they are not in the world they think they are in.

resolutions.move: Meridian: Agentic Appeals Factory + Denial-Prevention Stack (self-build, autonomy ladder)
resolutions.rationale: 12-24mo IT friction (Rule 3.2) bars production scale in T1; Vendor declined the anchor engagement (its own move sheet reserved Meridian for point solutions) and raided the build team, adding 3-6 months. Ambient/CDI already at production stage earns a small prevention gain within bounded movement; appeals CD 9 in the merits domain is real but undeployed at scale — Blue captures only 25-40% of the appeal-domain swing (D2 gap 1-2), enough to hold overturn rates flat against the -5pp/yr base-rate decline, not reverse Red's audit yield.

resolutions.move: Lakeview: Renewal-Window Process-Term Trade with RegionalMutual
resolutions.rationale: Contract terms bind at renewal (3.2) — the window was real, but leverage was 45%-of-book asymmetric and RegionalMutual arrived with its own squeeze. Signed: gold-card enrollment, API early-connect co-announcement, diluted code-level quarterly reporting. Refused: deemed-approval on SLA breach, timely-filing tolling. Conceded in the same paper: expanded prepay clinical-validation categories, shortened filing windows. Coalition-rails contingency appeals proceeded quietly at small scale.

resolutions.move: Prairie: Buy-Only Survival Package (contingency recovery + patient-AI routing)
resolutions.rationale: Buy-only is the correct base-rate play for a no-analytics actor and executed on schedule; backlog contingency recovery yields small found money at zero fixed cost. But W2 caps the patient-AI lane at niche volume (2%→~4% nationally), and RegionalMutual's squeeze terms landed on Prairie's renewal unmodified — Prairie's operating environment worsened even as its recovery machinery improved.

resolutions.move: Summit + coalition: Payer-Behavior Data Cooperative + CMS-0057-F first-mover automation
resolutions.rationale: Cooperative charter survived the gate in converted form and was signed with formation costs paid and zero T1 benefit claimed — honest per D2 §3. Summit's FHIR build completed, but W2's CMS enforcement-discretion posture left most payer endpoints attestation-grade: one production dyad (GovProgramCo-Summit), exactly the Da Vinci pilot-pair base rate. Gold-card petitions track the ~3% statutory uptake base rate — thin. Non-readiness documentation banked for the evidentiary ledger, but W2 regulators give it no immediate outlet.

resolutions.move: NationalCo: Frontier PI escalation on ASO post-pay
resolutions.rationale: D2 §1: CD ~10 vs Blue defense at ~4-5 on audit surfaces (14% claims-AI deployment base, builds not yet mature) — gap ≥3, 60-80% swing capture, durable until Blue's cooperative/self-build recompute CD. Payer-economics brief: ASO recoveries book as ~20% contingency fee revenue, no MLR drag, no conflict tax under D2. Post-pay, facility-facing focus avoided the churn-threshold roll (§2.2). Cost: +5-10% cumulative litigation-shock probability logged; one single-turn media flare; hospital-association abrasion recorded.

resolutions.move: NationalCo (lead): Employer Retention Shield — pre-emptive ASO Transparency Addendum
resolutions.rationale: W2 employer inertia delivered the unorganized majority: 3-year extensions signed across most in-window non-coalition accounts, stranding future Green leverage there through 2029. But Green organized faster than Red assumed — the 12-15 coalition jumbos refused the plain form, and live-RFP accounts settled on hybrids matching Red's own stated fallback: transparency yes, fee caps no, prospective clawback of fees on overturned recoveries under agreed methodology, shorter extensions. The dashboards Red granted now feed Green's audit file.

resolutions.move: RegionalMutual: Renewal-cycle squeeze with gold-card cover
resolutions.rationale: Friction rule favored the incumbent at renewal: Prairie signed as drafted; Lakeview signed modified, extracting API partnership, gold-card, and reporting concessions as the price. The gold-card program launched at trivial volume (~3% uptake base rate) and bought home-market cover cheaply. But the white-label NationalCo platform is inside its 12-24mo integration window — T1 tightening is contractual, not yet algorithmic; yield lands T2.

resolutions.move: GovProgramCo: Compliance-forward automation and the 2029 Stars ramp
resolutions.rationale: Cheapest clean win of the turn. Auto-approval of low-risk PA at the ~$0.05 electronic cost point (CAQH) raised auto-adjudication share with zero Stars friction; the individualized-determination scrub retires nH-Predict-shaped discovery risk before any plaintiff order arrives (litigation clocks show operational effect precedes legal resolution); the MA-tightening ramp is a free option keyed to the 2027 measurement year. W2's CMS discretion made early 0057-F compliance an optics surplus and handed GovProgramCo the only production API dyad.

resolutions.move: Stand up Purchaser Claims-Integrity Coalition + ASO Model Terms v1 into live RFPs
resolutions.rationale: Coalition formed with formation costs paid per D2 §3 — real legal/antitrust spend, zero T1 metric benefit, honestly budgeted. Terms bind only at renewal (3.2): hybrid signings achieved at live-RFP accounts (prospective overturn-clawback, transparency, scoped audit), but Red's extension shield stranded much of the non-coalition book past 2029 first. Broad bind arrives with the 2027-28 renewal cycle, T2.

resolutions.move: CAA fiduciary offensive: 408(b)(2)/claims-data demand letters
resolutions.rationale: The move's objective was the record, and the record now exists either way: NationalCo produced partially with logged proprietary objections; RegionalMutual produced more, on its addendum paper. Documented diligence improves Green's fiduciary posture immediately, independent of carrier behavior — the J&J/Wells Fargo standing dismissals cut against suing now, which Green correctly did not do. Litigation-predicate file open and growing.

resolutions.move: Direct-contracting pilot with Summit and Meridian on high-dispute episodes
resolutions.rationale: Summit signed fast — PA relief plus guaranteed volume is existential relief at 40 PAs/physician-week (AMA). Meridian's committee friction pushed its market to a late-T1 signature. Pilot-scale honored per 3.2; no episode economics until T2; TPA operational immaturity flagged. The strategic payload landed regardless: Green's defection threat is now on paper, which repriced every retention conversation Red had this turn.

resolutions.move: Independent forensic audit of PI vendor economics and duopoly conflict exposure
resolutions.rationale: Ownership mapping needed only public records and succeeded: Crucible's both-sides structure is now a documented, discoverable exhibit per the Vendor-conflict rule. The fee-vs-overturn matching half stalled on data access — complete only for accounts with pre-existing audit clauses. W2 media gave one business-press flare that decayed; the AG referral produced an informal inquiry that, on W2 base rates, likely closes without action. The exhibit's value is as T2-T3 ammunition, not T1 damage.

resolutions.move: Dual-front CMS-0057-F land grab (Sentinel PA / Overturn Engine)
resolutions.rationale: Both anchor assumptions missed: RegionalMutual bought intra-Red (NationalCo white-label) and NationalCo self-builds, so Red-side ARR is GovProgramCo modules plus mid-market carriers, not the nationals. Blue side landed Summit and Prairie backlog work, but Blue deliberately routed Prairie/Lakeview through Meridian's coalition rails to limit dependence. ARR still grows moderately — contingency pricing mechanically scales with a disputed-dollar pool that expanded this turn.

resolutions.move: PlanGuard: Green pre-emption / fiduciary armor
resolutions.rationale: The move's premise — Green stays unorganized 12-15 months — was wrong; the coalition formed inside the window and mandated an auditor with no commercial relationship to the duopoly, rejecting severability as adequate separation. Mid-market non-coalition sales are consolation revenue, not the audit-terms pen the move was built to capture. The product's existence is now itself an exhibit in Green's conflict file.

resolutions.move: Kill dispute-shrinking instruments + talent raids
resolutions.rationale: Raids succeeded — labor market tightness (Brief A §4) makes poaching credible; 2-3 SIU leaders moved, and Meridian's build slipped 3-6 months, a real extension of Rule 3.2 friction. Lobbying, however, pushed on an open door: in W2, dispute-shrinking legislation was going nowhere anyway (4-8 state passages across the whole game, 3-7yr lag), so the spend bought little marginal protection. NationalCo relationship bruised; non-solicit friction logged.

resolutions.move: Cross-side data flywheel (Payer Playbook / Provider Signal)
resolutions.rationale: Launched at the 14-month mark with modest uptake: Provider Signal found thin demand (NationalCo buys nothing strategic; RegionalMutual sourced intra-coalition); Payer Playbook sells to Blue but now competes with Blue's own converted cooperative. The strategic cost exceeded the revenue: the holding-level shared-services telemetry agreement makes the conflict operational rather than structural — White raises the conflict-exposure flag to its highest T1 setting, discoverable by any cell in T2-T3 proceedings.

turns.bluePosture: ASYMMETRIC ESCALATION ON FAVORABLE GROUND. Blue does not fight Red claim-for-claim across all domains — under D2 physics that is a CD contest we lose in payment-integrity pattern-mining, where payers hold the data advantage. Blue escalates hard in the two domains where provider Capability Differential is structurally highest: (1) the appeal-merits domain, where we hold the full clinical record Red cannot see (Data access 3/3), overturn base rates of 55-65% prove the merits run our way (Regulatory/contractual 1/1), and 40% of denials are currently never appealed — meaning the single largest pool of contested dollars on the board is money Red is keeping only because nobody shows up. Attacking the non-appeal gap converts Red's automated denial volume into our revenue-recovery volume at ~$57/claim cost against claims worth multiples of that. (2) The upstream prevention domain — ambient documentation, CDI, clean-claim automation — where denials die before they exist and no arms-race counter is possible. Simultaneously we begin the one capability-leapfrog investment D2 rewards: pooled payer-behavior data, paid for now so CD recomputes in our favor by T2-T3. Prairie and Summit ride coalition/vendor rails; nobody self-builds who cannot. All scale claims are T2 claims; T1 is procurement, build-start, and renewal positioning, consistent with 12-24 month friction.

Red escalates at maximum capability where the economics are unambiguous and the abrasion channels are quiet — post-pay payment integrity on ASO volume, where every recovered dollar books ~20 cents of near-pure-margin fee revenue with zero MLR drag — while deliberately cooling the member-visible surfaces (prior-auth denials on active care, MA post-acute cuts) that feed CTM complaints, state AI-UM bills, and churn-threshold rolls. Under D2, our CD advantage is real: frontier models, full adjudication data, national deployment scale versus a provider base with 14% claims-AI penetration and 12-24 month build cycles. We press that gap for two turns of durable swing capture. The one strategic threat that dwarfs PI fee income is losing jumbo ASO accounts, so we spend this turn pre-emptively locking the employer book before Green organizes — on our paper, at our fee structure. Litigation hygiene is absolute: no written denial targets, no volume quotas, individualized-determination sign-off layers on every algorithmic pathway, because discovery of a target memo is the only cheap way we lose.

turns.narrative:
Turn 2 was the turn the money changed lanes. NationalCo read Green's clawback riders correctly and moved its integrity engine upstream: a dollar never paid generates no overturned recovery, so the prepay validation layer now runs on high-dollar facility claims across NationalCo's book and RegionalMutual's newly cut-over production stack. The pivot worked — but at the coalition dozen it collided head-on with the renewal wave, and the fee schedule Red brought to the table came back marked up with Green's account-by-account caps, an auditable avoided-spend methodology, and escrow seasoning. Red bought its three-year locks; Green billed for them, and the first clawback settlements on T1 fees — lowballed, partial, precedent-setting — were paid this turn. Two coalition jumbos walked to RFP anyway.

Blue stopped losing without yet winning. Meridian's appeals engine hit production inside the 12-24 month window and began strip-mining the never-appealed 40%; overturn rates on fought claims held against the falling base rate and cost-per-touch fell materially. But the shared utility's tenants onboarded mid-year, the cooperative's lagged aggregates describe a post-pay audit pattern Red is now abandoning, and RegionalMutual's cutover plus the T1 filing windows kept Lakeview and Prairie under water. Coalition leakage: arrested, not reversed. The quiet structural event was the Employer-Directed Data Pass-Through Rider — RegionalMutual could not refuse plan sponsors their own data on the record Green had built, and home-market audit intensity now flows to a conflict-free auditor on a schedule.

GovProgramCo executed the coldest calculation on the board: MA intensity stepped up in the first measurement year freed of the complaints, appeals, and disenrollment Stars measures, wrapped in physician signatures that sailed through the state's thin first audit cycle. The economics cleared. The IRE overturn statistics, Prairie's docket filings, and a patient-AI channel now assisting 6-7% of contested determinations are all compounding silently in the shock accumulator — landing window mostly past the scoring horizon, which is exactly the bet.

Vendor had its worst good turn. Mid-market Blue ARR grew through GPO channels, but the table-actor mid-market went to Meridian's no-contingency utility, Red terminated it on clean paper, and the Green flip died on arrival — the conflict-free-auditor pitch itself became the newest page in Green's exhibit, filed mid-inquiry.

The environment stayed W2 molasses: CMS extended enforcement discretion into 2029, the AI-UM audits were desk exercises, the benefits trade press flared over the anchor CAA lawsuit and moved on, and the AG kept the file open and did nothing. The tinder pile grew; nothing lit it.
env: CMS extended CMS-0057-F enforcement discretion into 2029 for attesting plans (W2 posture: discretion through T4-T5); trade press noted GovProgramCo's three production provider dyads as the compliance showcase — general media ignored the story.

The enacted AI-UM statute ran its first audit cycle: desk audits, two corrective-action letters to unnamed smaller plans, no fines. GovProgramCo's physician-signature wrapper passed cleanly; Prairie's structured complaint filings entered the docket with no action this turn — symbolic enforcement, exactly the modal year-one outcome.

Media roll (1-in-2): HIT, trade-scope only. Benefits trade press covered the anchor CAA claims-data lawsuit and the coalition audit sweep for one cycle; no national pickup, flare decayed by turn end. Audience effect: fiduciary committees noticed; one non-coalition employer demanded audit rights (W2 employer inertia otherwise held).

Court roll (1-in-4): MISS — no consequential ruling. Lokken-class discovery ground forward on the litigation clock; the Green anchor suit's MTD will not resolve until 2029; one unrelated algorithmic-denial matter settled confidentially, cash-only, no process terms.

State AG: the informal dual-sided-vendor inquiry stayed open but inactive, now fed by Green's audit-supplement referral and by Vendor's own mid-inquiry restructuring filing (logged as a discoverable timing fact). W2 reactive posture: no action absent a fresh shock; the file is thicker, not hotter.

Patient-side appeal AI (exogenous): assisted share of contested determinations grew from ~4% to ~6-7%, still concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members; MA post-acute denials emerged as the channel's highest-yield target category. Vendor's white-label stake closed, making the channel's growth partly Vendor revenue — and its overturns still feed Green's clawback ledger.

turns.narrative:
The scoring turn ended not with a collision but with a sorting: every actor finally paid or collected on positions built in 2026-28. The most consequential convergence was accidental — Lakeview walked into its renewal armed with the auditor record, and RegionalMutual walked in already intending to sell the concessions automation had made costless. The deal closed fast: timely-filing parity at last, a deemed-approval SLA on gold-carded sets, partial 85%-threshold expansion — priced in a three-year lock and Lakeview's withdrawal as complainant (White converted the withdrawal term; the docket record itself is beyond private contract). Prairie got the schedule unprompted. It was the best paper a Blue archetype signed all game, and RegionalMutual still profited from it.

Upstream, the machine war narrowed to formats. Meridian's first-pass engine reached production inside the window and began compiling Red's own published criteria into clean claims; at guarantee-converted coalition accounts NationalCo rationally signed machine-readable delivery, since a correct claim now helps its trend guarantee rather than starving a contingency fee. But RegionalMutual's quarterly logic rotation kept the cooperative's aggregates one cycle stale, and NationalCo's expansion into professional and outpatient surgical surfaces opened fresh ground where Blue's engine starts a year behind. Leakage bent — moderately, late, and unevenly.

GovProgramCo executed the cleanest exit of the game: post-acute taper, 72-hour auto-reversal of its weakest denials, and its FHIR stack white-labeled across the coalition just as CMS let discretion lapse into corrective-action letters. The accumulator kept growing — three state statutes now enacted, the anchor CAA suit surviving its motion in part on Green's documented record — but everything lands 2031-plus. Red settled the surviving claims cash-only, confidential, no process terms: the W2 signature, performed on schedule.

Green banked the quieter win. The split award landed both jumbos in the scoring window — a priced comparator Red must now bid against everywhere — and the prepay true-up rider bound at coalition accounts, converting Red's upstream fee pool into contingent revenue even where settlements came in low. The plan-sponsored appeal benefit pushed assisted contests to roughly a tenth of determinations, though White ruled prepay documentation review largely non-member-visible: no churn roll fired.

Vendor got most of what a seller needs. The demerger executed, the AG stayed dormant behind the pre-brief, and the PI arm closed to a non-table strategic with an inquiry-sized escrow. The appeals arm was still unsold at the horizon, and Green declined the advocacy pitch a third time — passive sponsor economics pending sale is not severance. Final ordering on own-book economics: Green, then Red and Blue nearly level — Red richer cumulatively, Blue steeper at the close — Vendor solvent, separated, and half-exited.
env: CMS (scheduled): 0057-F enforcement discretion lapsed at end-2029; CMS issued corrective-action-plan letters to non-attesting laggards — no penalties, no Stars linkage this cycle (W2: real teeth post-horizon). The Red coalition attested from GovProgramCo's white-labeled production stack; the showcase strategy paid exactly when designed to.

Courts (litigation clock, not a roll): the anchor CAA claims-data suit's MTD was granted in part and denied in part in 2029 — Green's actual pass-through data record distinguished the J&J/Wells Fargo standing failures on the data-access and fee-transparency counts. Late 2030 the surviving claims settled confidentially, cash-only, no process commitments: the W2 modal ending. Lokken-class matters remained in discovery with no merits resolution inside the horizon.
Court random roll (1-in-4): MISS — no additional consequential ruling; two copycat algorithmic-denial suits filed, expected to resolve on the same quiet pattern.

Regulatory roll (1-in-3): HIT, symbolic — two further states enacted SB1120-class physician-review AI-UM statutes (game cumulative: three of W2's 4-8 band). Rulemaking pends, enforcement budgets thin, no ERISA reach; earliest operational bite 2031-2033. The first-enacted state's second audit cycle issued one small fine — single digits, as W2 specifies.

Media roll (1-in-2): HIT, trade-scope, single cycle — benefits and business trade press covered the coalition jumbos' split award and the quarterly comparator as an employer-market story ('the plan sponsors who fired their carrier's audit shop'). Decayed by turn end; residue was a handful of non-coalition sponsors executing Pass-Through Riders through their consultants.

State AG: the dual-sided-vendor file remained open and inactive through the horizon. Vendor's pre-briefed demerger was logged as cooperation; Green's true-up audit findings thickened the file once more. W2 posture holds: absent a fresh shock, the file trends toward quiet closure post-game — tinder to the end, never fire.

Patient-side appeal AI (exogenous + Green sponsorship): assisted share of contested determinations reached ~9-10%, the top of the W2 band — the plan-sponsored benefit pushed a niche channel to its structural ceiling. Per-appeal MA yield declined as GovProgramCo vacated post-acute; commercial prepay-related appeals became the channel's new growth category, feeding Green's true-up ledger.

Labor: Vendor's final pre-exit raids fizzled against NationalCo's counter-recruiting; demerger uncertainty reversed the flow, with exception-management and SIU talent leaving Vendor for payer and provider in-house teams. Wage inflation in exception roles persisted on both sides — symmetric admin drag, paid in each cell's own ledger per D2, never canceled.
