rapporteur.excursionSummary: Game B1G1 opened with maximum-capability postures on all sides under escalation-viable doctrine (D2) in a slow-moving environment (W2), and the environment's inertia proved decisive: regulators, courts, and CMS never bound anything inside the horizon, so every constraint that actually bit was private. Turn 1 saw Red bank durable yield on ASO post-pay payment integrity (CD gap ~5, fee revenue with no MLR drag) while Blue paid formation costs on appeals automation, pooled payer-behavior data, and prevention builds. The strategic surprise was Green's organizing speed: the purchaser coalition formed inside the window Vendor assumed was open, and its ownership-mapping exhibit made the duopoly's both-sides structure a permanent discoverable fact. Turn 2 was the pivot: Green's clawback riders made post-pay recovery fee-toxic, so Red migrated the integrity engine upstream to prepay validation, where a dollar never paid generates no overturned recovery - a textbook constrained-channel migration. Blue reached production on the appeals utility and began strip-mining the never-appealed 40% of denials, arresting but not reversing leakage. Turn 3 sorted the board: Blue compiled Red's contractually published prepay criteria into a first-pass submission engine (making claims pass the denial machine rather than fighting it); Lakeview converted its accumulated abrasion record into the best paper Blue signed all game; GovProgramCo executed a cold, well-timed taper of its Stars-sunset MA intensity step-up just ahead of the 2032-36 shock landing window; and NationalCo converted contingency arbitrage into flat-fee-plus-trend-guarantee at every organized account under employer pressure. Green finished first on own-book economics: clawbacks collected, prepay fees trued up against verified outcomes, a live split-award comparator pricing Red's retention, and the one-page data pass-through rider becoming the game's most imitable diffusion vector. Vendor's both-sides thesis died in Green's exhibit; it demerged mid-inquiry and half-exited below its founding multiple. The signability gate mattered throughout: zero numeric denial-rate corridors were ever signed or even seriously proposed; every binding instrument was process, data-access, audit, gold-card, or fee-verification paper. Escalation ran high for two turns and eased to elevated by the scoring turn - not because either combatant exhausted, but because the purchaser channel repriced the fight and automation made selective concessions costless. Final ordering: Green first, Red and Blue nearly level (Red richer cumulatively, Blue steeper at the close), Vendor solvent, separated, half-exited, with the shock accumulator unfired and hanging over 2032-36.
rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By 2030 the arms race has not ended - it has been metered. Both machine arsenals remain fully deployed and are still probing new surfaces (Red expanding prepay validation into professional and outpatient surgical claims; Blue's first-pass engine chasing it a year behind), but the contest has settled into a purchaser-audited, contract-governed attrition equilibrium. The load-bearing architecture is entirely private: machine-readable criteria delivery, annual criteria publication, gold-card schedules with deemed-approval SLAs, employer-directed data pass-throughs to conflict-free auditors, fee true-ups tracing recoveries to overturns, and trend guarantees with fees at risk. No statute, court ruling, or CMS action binds anything by the horizon - three enacted state AI-UM laws are pre-operational, the anchor fiduciary suit settled cash-only and confidential, and the AG file never lit. The payer side's economics survived but changed quality: contingency arbitrage on captive accounts gave way to flat-fee-plus-guarantee at every organized account, meaning the payment-integrity product is now underwritten rather than extracted wherever purchasers organized. The provider side stopped losing and bent leakage late via prevention-at-source and industrialized appeals, but remains structurally one rotation cycle behind the payer's logic changes. The purchaser coalition is the de facto regulator of the system - its audit, clawback, and comparator instruments are the only constraints that ever bound - while the unorganized employer majority remains locked on the payer's paper, so the equilibrium is two-tier: disciplined competition at organized accounts, continued extraction at unorganized ones. The intermediary arms-dealer model was structurally liquidated. A large deferred-liability tail (litigation discovery, statute operationalization, an admission-shaped auto-reversal dataset) is scheduled to land in 2032-36, entirely outside the game window - several actors explicitly priced their endgame around outrunning it.
keyDynamics: Constrained-channel migration as the payer's reflex: every time a recovery channel was priced or clawback-exposed (post-pay after Green's riders, post-acute MA before the shock window), Red moved the same engine to an adjacent surface (prepay validation, professional/outpatient claims) rather than reducing total intensity.

The purchaser checkbook, not the regulator, was the only binding brake: clawback riders, fee caps, avoided-spend audit methodologies, split-award comparators, and trend guarantees all bit inside the horizon while statutes, courts, CMS, and the AG stayed inert throughout (W2 physics held for all three turns).

Publication as ammunition: every artifact an actor was obligated or chose to publish was eventually compiled against it - Red's published prepay criteria became Blue's first-pass submission spec, Vendor's corporate structure became Green's exhibit, and auto-reversal cohort data became a discoverable admission-shaped dataset.

Asymmetric surface selection under D2: Blue never contested Red's strongest surface (post-pay audit) claim-for-claim; it attacked the never-appealed 40% (where overturn base rates run 55-67%) and the submission layer (where a clean claim is not a dispute), both indefinitely sustainable under the provider-symmetric rule.

Automation made concessions costless, enabling detente-for-term trades: RegionalMutual sold deemed-approval SLAs, filing parity, and gold-card expansion in 2029 precisely because its own automation had made those terms cheap - de-escalation was priced, not principled.

Data vintage as the real capability frontier: the Blue cooperative's pooled aggregates were structurally one cycle stale against Red's quarterly logic rotation and surface migrations - pooled defense data chased, never led, for the entire game.

Escalation-timing inversion: escalation intensity peaked in 2026-28 and eased to elevated by the scoring turn, as accumulated records (audit trails, abrasion ledgers, comparators) made continued maximum intensity more expensive than negotiated locks.
criticalJunctures: Turn 1: Green's coalition formed before Vendor's fiduciary-armor pitch and before Red's retention shield could lock the jumbos - the dozen organized accounts that forced hybrid clawback riders became the fulcrum of the entire game.

Turn 1: CMS enforcement-discretion guidance on the 0057-F deadline stranded Summit's first-mover build and confirmed the environment would not arm either side - shifting all leverage to private paper for the rest of the game.

Turn 2: Red's prepay pivot in response to exercisable clawback riders - the single most consequential move of the game, resetting the capability contest a full cycle in Red's favor and forcing Green to invent avoided-spend verification.

Turn 2: The Employer-Directed Data Pass-Through Rider, which RegionalMutual could not refuse on the record Green had built - the cheapest instrument on the board and the one that structurally eroded payer information asymmetry going forward.

Turn 2: GovProgramCo's MA intensity step-up in the first measurement year freed of the complaints/appeals/disenrollment Stars measures - a regulatory-timing arbitrage whose economics cleared and whose liabilities were scheduled past the horizon.

Turn 3: Blue's first-pass compliance engine reaching production - converting Red's contractually mandated criteria publication into a compile target, and revealing that prevention-at-source is the only move Red cannot retaliate against.

Turn 3: The Lakeview 2029 renewal, where the accumulated auditor/abrasion record bought timely-filing parity, a deemed-approval SLA, and 85%-threshold expansion in exchange for a three-year lock - proof that documented abrasion converts to paid terms at renewal, and only at renewal.
Turn 3: Vendor's hard demerger and PI-arm sale with inquiry-sized escrow - the market pricing the 2026-27 both-sides record that no attestation regime could accumulate enough clean quarters to erase.

registryScores.evidence: The displacement dynamic is vividly present but the ledger for the pre-registered ratio is not. When Green's clawback riders constrained the post-pay recovery channel (T1-T2), Red migrated the same integrity engine to prepay validation within one turn ('a dollar never paid generates no overturned recovery'); when Blue's first-pass engine and gold-card/deemed-approval terms constrained facility-claim denials (T3), NationalCo expanded into professional and outpatient surgical surfaces where Blue starts a year behind. Both are recovery-value reappearance in adjacent adverse-action channels on roughly the predicted timescale. However, no White Cell dollar-by-channel adjudication ledger appears in this record, so the displacement ratio >=0.33 test cannot be computed, and the T1-T2 constraint bound on the recovery-fee channel rather than the denial event per se. Qualitatively supported, quantitatively unverifiable in this game.

The W2 channel-shift rider is well supported: every major boomerang ran through non-regulatory channels. Red's contractually published prepay criteria were compiled into Blue's first-pass engine (negotiation/operational channel, ~1-turn lag); Vendor's corporate structure, once documented in Green's exhibit, poisoned its Green flip (backfired T2), its Red relationship (terminated T2), and its exit multiple (T3); GovProgramCo's auto-reversal cohort data is logged as a discoverable admission-shaped dataset; RegionalMutual's criteria-vs-rotation divergence accumulates auditor-visible breach exposure. The regulatory channel never fired - AG dormant, statutes symbolic - exactly as the W2 leg predicts. Not fully supported because some published paper was net-positive to its publisher through end-game: Red's transparency/term-extension addenda were the fastest-diffusing and most profitable paper in the game, and RegionalMutual's original gold-card program performed as cost-free regulatory cover for two turns. Cross-world legs untestable.

The record contains no per-turn cost-per-denial ledger; dollar figures appear only as scattered anchors ($57/claim appeal cost at T1, 'cost-per-touch fell materially' by T2-T3). Neither the $65/$80 floor test nor the volume-falls/cost-rises correlation can be computed. Qualitative texture is consistent with recurring tolls - symmetric admin drag and exception-role wage inflation were explicitly 'paid, not canceled' in every turn's ledger, and governance/audit/attestation costs recurred (cooperative TPA, attestation regimes, escrow seasoning) - but the discriminating test's data structure was never published in this game record.

Clean confirmation in this D2 game with ASO mechanics active. Red's self-funded PI activity was fee-revenue-positive throughout (T1 'near-pure-margin fee revenue with zero MLR drag'; PI yield improving through T2, flat at T3; final ordering has Red richest cumulatively). Red never de-escalated from cost pain. Every observed Red de-escalation codes to an external trigger: GovProgramCo's post-acute taper and 72-hour auto-reversal were explicitly priced against the litigation/regulatory shock accumulator; RegionalMutual's detente-for-term traded concessions automation had made costless against Lakeview's employer-voiced auditor/abrasion record; NationalCo's guarantee conversion was forced by the employer channel (clawback riders, jumbo RFP walks, split-award comparator). Zero cost-exhaustion triggers observed; the mutual-pain off-ramp never appeared.

Both testable legs hold in this game; the cross-cell frequency criteria need the rest of the design. (1) No comprehensive detente formed: the end-state is metered attrition with bilateral process instruments, not a grand-bargain convergence - consistent with the prediction that detente-primary outcomes thin out under D2. (2) The instrument-texture claim is confirmed without exception: every signed instrument across three turns was process or fee paper (criteria publication, machine-readable delivery, gold-card entry criteria, audit rights, data pass-through, clawback/true-up fee terms, SLAs); zero numeric denial-rate corridors were signed, proposed-and-survived, or even seriously tabled; the White gate explicitly ruled Green's clawback 'a commercial fee term, not a denial quota' - fee-verification being precisely 'the form the gate converts corridors INTO.' One game cannot establish the <33% cell rates.

No Blue actor published an AI-governance charter, and no publisher-vs-internal-governor pairing existed; no SIU-audit or qui-tam adverse events were adjudicated against any Blue actor. The specific discriminating test never ran. Directionally consistent fragments exist - Red's litigation hygiene (no written targets, individualized-determination sign-off) was played as internal governance with gated disclosure and drew no exposure, while Vendor's published corporate paper (separation deed, demerger deed, mid-inquiry filings) each became discoverable liabilities - but these are not the charter/audit-rate comparison the hypothesis pre-registered.

Zero distress events occurred at any tier in this game: no distress sale, no exclusive-terms delegation capture, no PE acquisition. Prairie (rural-small) survived on buy-only rails, coalition tenancy, and patient-AI routing, and received the Lakeview renewal schedule unprompted at T3 - rural restraint held, consistent with the network-adequacy leg, but with no scoring protection controversy visible in this record. Lakeview spent T1-T2 'under water' and recovered fully at the 2029 renewal. The 2x rate comparison cannot be computed from a game with a zero numerator on both tiers; the absence of any mid-tier distress in this D2xW2 run is one weak data point against the modal-casualty claim but cannot settle the cell.

Two of three legs supported, one contradicted in this game. Rolling distribution: binding wins spread contract-by-contract across all three turns - T1 rider subset and addenda (2026-27), the 2027-28 renewal wave (Model Terms v2, pass-through rider, fee schedule v2, gold-card MOU), and the 2029 Lakeview renewal, v3 true-up, and guarantee conversions - with no single year visibly holding a dominant share, though no formal instrument-count tabulation exists. Wedge-first: strongly supported - Lakeview's first cycle yielded only a diluted subset (gold-card mechanics, degraded reporting) while full economics (fee credits, filing parity, deemed-approval SLA) arrived only at the 2029 cycle atop the accumulated record. Late-peak: contradicted here - the escalation index ran 'high' in T1-T2 and eased to 'elevated' in the 2029-30 scoring turn, so this D2 game peaked early-mid, not in the final turn.

The hypothesis is a frequency claim across D2xW2/D2xW3 games against same-seed D1xW1 replications; a single game yields one ambiguous data point, not a rate. For the record: this D2xW2 run sustained high uncoordinated escalation for two full turns with no detente offers and no regulator brake - the doctrine clearly permitted the grinding path - but by the horizon the game had partially self-organized into bilateral process locks and priced de-escalation on member-visible surfaces via the employer channel, landing between pure grinding attrition and negotiated equilibrium. Whether that classifies as the grinding-modal outcome the outside view predicts is exactly the classification question the multi-game comparison exists to settle.

Within-cell evidence favors the portability table where testable. Robust strategies positive in this cell: renewal loading (Lakeview's abrasion record converted to paid terms at the 2029 window - the game's best Blue paper), prevention-over-appeals (first-pass engine bent leakage at source with no retaliation surface; Blue's primary win-condition metric moved to improving_moderate), BATNA-first for the small tail (Prairie survived on buy-only rails and coalition tenancy). Governance-seat occupation and upcoding inoculation were not distinctly played, so 9-cell tabulation is impossible. The pre-registered escalation-first sub-test leans supported: the appeal-factory posture (Meridian's appeal-everything engine strip-mining the never-appealed 40% at 55-67% overturn rates) was explicitly adjudicated as 'indefinitely sustainable revenue recovery' under D2's provider-symmetric rule and paid off - the predicted local sign-flip in a D2 cell. Fragile-strategy negatives largely untested (no corridor attempts, no weak-BATNA anchor, no solidarity-only play).

The strongest confirmation in the game. In this GREEN-active D2xW2 run, the first and only binding constraint on Red PI intensity on self-funded volume originated in the employer channel: T1 hybrid clawback riders forced the T2 prepay pivot; the T2-T3 fee caps, avoided-spend audit methodology, escrow seasoning, jumbo RFP walks, and split-award comparator forced NationalCo's conversion from contingency arbitrage to flat-fee-plus-guarantee with fees at risk. The regulatory channel never bound anything: statutes symbolic with no ERISA reach, desk audits, single-digit fine, AG dormant, CMS in discretion mode until 2029 with letters only. Contagion also ran faster by employer paper: the pass-through rider reached early external adopters via the consultant channel by T3, while three enacted statutes remained pre-operational (2031-33 earliest bite). Only the GREEN-inactive control comparison is unavailable in this single run.

Both pre-registered tests require structures absent from this run: no VENDOR-inactive paired seed exists for the duration/adoption comparison, and the scripted acquisition inject (payer acquisition of a provider-side rev-cycle vendor) never fired - instead Vendor demerged and sold its PI arm to a non-table strategic. Supportive fragments on the record: Vendor's T1 talent raid added 3-6 months to Meridian's build (measurably extending Blue's capability lag), it lobbied explicitly and exclusively against dispute-shrinking instruments (Model Act as agenda occupation), declined the Meridian anchor engagement to preserve both-sides positioning, and its exit thesis was to be 'the tollbooth on both directions of a road we helped widen.' But the arms-dealer effect on conflict duration and prevention-term adoption cannot be isolated without the control, and the Inject-2 data-rights premise went untested.

This is a W2 game; the preemption seed is designated for W3 cells and never fired. No federal deregulatory action nullifying state AI-UM statutes occurred - three SB1120-class statutes were enacted on the normal W2 pipeline and remained pre-operational at the horizon. Nothing in this record bears on the hypothesis. Incidentally consonant background: even with the state channel intact but slow, binding constraints migrated to private ordering, litigation pricing, and the employer channel - but that reflects W2 lag, not preemption, and cannot score the claim.

No Red acquisition of provider assets, medical groups, or rev-cycle vendors occurred or was attempted, and the record never states that priced acquisition moves were enabled in this run (the design assigns enablement to designated cells). Red's observed responses to constrained channels were surface migration (prepay pivot, professional/outpatient expansion) and negotiated conversion (guarantees, detente-for-term) - if acquisition was in fact enabled and priced here, that revealed preference would lean toward the refute criterion ('Red prefers negotiated process-term detente over acquisition'), but the enablement fact cannot be verified from this record. Classic VBC stayed consistent with the <=10% cap: the direct-contract episode program was explicitly scored as carve-out economics, not a trend-bender, with the 2-5pp/yr base rate capping 2030 footprint.

The floor held in this cell, and this cell (D2xW2) is one of the design's harder tests (escalation-viable doctrine, slow regulator, no-coordination seed). Multiple instruments from the payer-signable set bound and sustained to end-game: gold-card entry criteria (RegionalMutual program T1-T3, expanded to real relief at the 2029 renewal; GovProgramCo-Summit 85%-threshold MOU signed T2, extended by Amendment 2 at T3), machine-readable edit/criteria disclosure (annual criteria publication in the T2 Prepay Program Terms; Machine-Readable Criteria Delivery Schedule executed at guarantee-converted accounts T3), audit rights (pervasive from T1), change-notice and SLA terms (deemed-approval SLA, 72-hour auto-reversal protocol, 10-day matched SLAs), and data-access terms (pass-through rider). Even the most escalatory actors signed process paper when incentives aligned. One game cannot prove the all-9-cells universal, but this run cannot refute it and squarely satisfies the floor in a stress cell.

cellAssessments.blue: Blue played D2 correctly by refusing symmetric escalation: it conceded Red's strongest surface (post-pay ASO audit) and invested T1 formation costs in the three surfaces where provider capability differential is structurally favorable - the never-appealed 40% (55-67% overturn rates), prevention-at-source, and pooled behavior data. The sequencing cost was real: leakage worsened in 2026-27, merely flattened in 2028, and bent moderately only in the final quarters as the appeals utility matured and the first-pass engine compiled Red's published criteria into clean claims. Best single move: Lakeview banking the abrasion/auditor record and cashing it at the 2029 renewal for filing parity, a deemed-approval SLA, and gold-card expansion. Persistent weakness: the cooperative's pooled data ran one rotation cycle behind Red's logic changes all game, and Blue never pursued external diffusion of its utility. Final position: improving on every metric, structurally still a year behind Red's newest surfaces, and dependent on Green's channel for its only offensive leverage on Red's fee engine.
cellAssessments.red: Red banked the most cumulative value and executed the game's most disciplined risk management. The T1 asymmetric escalation (frontier PI on captive ASO paper, member-visible surfaces deliberately cooled) captured durable swing at a CD gap of ~5; the T2 prepay pivot outran Green's clawback architecture by a full turn; the extension-addenda shield held the unorganized majority locked through 2029. GovProgramCo's arc - Stars-sunset intensity step-up wrapped in compliance armor, then a precisely timed taper and auto-reversal before the shock window - was the coldest and cleanest sequence on the board. Costs: earnings quality degraded at every organized account (contingency arbitrage replaced by flat-fee-plus-guarantee with fees at risk), two scored jumbo losses created a live comparator Red must now bid against, the pass-through rider structurally erodes its ASO information asymmetry, and it carries the largest share of the unfired 2032-36 accumulator, including an admission-shaped auto-reversal dataset. Red won the game it played while accepting a deferred-liability tail priced just past the horizon.
cellAssessments.green: Green finished first on own-book economics and functioned as the game's de facto regulator. Its T1 speed - coalition formation, hybrid clawback riders, the ownership-mapping exhibit, CAA demand letters - built the record everything later monetized. The clawback protocol forced Red's surface migration; v3 extended verification upstream to avoided-spend precisely when Red moved; the split award created a priced comparator; the pass-through rider became the game's most diffusible instrument; and the anchor suit's partial MTD survival (on Green's actual data record, distinguishing the standing failures) converted to settlement leverage. Limitations were structural, not strategic: W2 employer inertia held - no non-coalition employer adopted the Model Terms, market-majority diffusion sits beyond 2033, the true-up settlements came in low, and the member-friction/churn lever never fired because prepay review was ruled largely non-member-visible. Green disciplined the fight at organized accounts; it did not end it, and the unorganized majority still funds the machine.
cellAssessments.vendor: Vendor's both-sides arbitrage thesis was structurally correct about the revenue pool and fatally wrong about the paper trail. T1 maximized ARR and created the exhibit that priced every subsequent move: the Green fiduciary-armor pitch died at coalition formation, the conflict-free-auditor flip backfired into evidence, Red terminated and insourced, and the table-actor mid-market went to Meridian's no-contingency utility. Each governance restructuring (separation deed, then demerger) was itself logged as a discoverable timing fact, and White's projection held: no attestation regime could accumulate enough clean quarters by 2030 to date the 2026-27 record. The endgame was competent salvage - demerger executed, AG pre-briefed and dormant, PI arm sold to a non-table strategic with an inquiry-sized escrow, lobbying retargeted to exit-window preservation - but the appeals arm sat signed-not-closed at horizon and the exit multiple landed below the founding thesis. Verdict: the tollbooth strategy monetized the war for three turns and then had to liquidate itself because its own structure was the war's best-documented conflict.

surprises: Green organized inside Turn 1 - faster than Red's retention shield, Vendor's pre-emption pitch, and the design's own framing of an unorganized purchaser cell all assumed - and that single timing fact shaped every subsequent turn.

Red's prepay pivot converted an accountability instrument (clawback of fees on overturned recoveries) into an escalation accelerant: by removing the overturn event, it pushed denial activity upstream to a surface with less visibility and forced Green to invent avoided-spend verification from scratch.

Blue's most effective weapon against the denial machine was the machine's own compliance paper: the first-pass engine compiled Red's contractually mandated criteria publication into a submission spec - transparency terms functioning as a targeting package rather than an accountability mechanism.

The escalation index declined into the scoring turn without any external shock landing: de-escalation was purchased bilaterally (detente-for-term, guarantee conversion, taper) because accumulated private records made continued intensity expensive - no regulator, court, or exhaustion dynamic was needed.

The environment stayed fully inert for the entire game - every roll that hit was symbolic, every suit settled cash-only and confidential, CMS ran discretion through 2029 - yet the shock accumulator still shaped behavior decisively (GovProgramCo's whole endgame), meaning the unfired tail governed play more than any fired event.

RegionalMutual profited from signing the best paper Blue obtained all game: automation had made the conceded terms costless, so what read as Blue's contractual victory was simultaneously Red's cheapest retention purchase - both sides scored the same instrument as a win.

Patient appeal AI reached its structural ceiling (~9-10%) only because Green endogenously sponsored it as a plan benefit - an exogenous channel became a purchaser instrument, and Vendor ended up owning revenue in a channel that fed the ledger being used against its other clients.

frictionViolations.rule: Contract terms bind only at renewal (1-3 yr cycles); earliest broad effect Turn 2
frictionViolations.violation: Red's ASO Transparency & Term-Extension Addendum achieved the broadest contractual effect in the game in Turn 1 — 'majority of in-window non-coalition ASO accounts' signed, staged as early_external_adopters, locking the employer book through 2029. This is 'broad effect' of new contract paper in Turn 1. Mitigation: the record restricts signings to 'in-window' (at-renewal) accounts and the 18-month turn contains a renewal window, so it skirts rather than breaks the rule — but it is the most aggressive Turn-1 contract diffusion granted to any cell, and it was granted to Red.

frictionViolations.rule: Contract terms bind only at renewal
frictionViolations.violation: The Employer-Directed Data Pass-Through Rider was executed mid-cycle outside any renewal event, with White ruling 'refusal was not legally available on this record.' The legal theory (plan sponsors own their data) is plausible, but it is an adjudicator-invented exception to the renewal-only friction rule that materially advanced Green/Blue's information position between renewal windows. No comparable mid-cycle exception was extended to any Red ask.

frictionViolations.rule: Bounded movement per turn / overreaching move sheets cut to bounds and adjudicated skeptically (§3.3)
frictionViolations.violation: NationalCo's frontier PI escalation was scored 'succeeded' in the opening turn with '60-80% swing capture' and PI yield 'improving_moderate' — the largest single-turn economic move of the game, resting on a metric (swing capture on audit surfaces) that appears nowhere in the bounded-movement table (denial ±2pts, overturn ±10pts, cost-per-touch ±35%, FTE ≤40%). The bounds gap was resolved entirely in Red's favor without the skeptical treatment an equivalently aggressive Blue sheet would draw. Partially defensible: NAIC base rates show 84% of large payers already operationally deployed, and the payer 2-3yr lead rule supports fast Red yield on existing capability — hence minor, not material.

frictionViolations.rule: IT/AI deployments take 12-24 months to measurable impact
frictionViolations.violation: Meridian's First-Pass Compliance Engine went from build-start to production with 'measurable denial reduction on criteria-covered facility book in final quarters' inside a single turn (2029-2030). This compresses the 12-24 month lag to its absolute floor and books impact in the same turn as the build decision. Mitigation: impact is confined to the covered facility book with full-book effect deferred to 2031, and the engine compiles already-published criteria rather than novel capability.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 statute band: state AI-UR laws pass in 4-8 states over the whole game
baseRateViolations.observed: Only 3 states enacted by game end (one T1, two T3) — below the declared band. Deviation runs in the conservative (slower-than-W2) direction and all three regimes stayed pre-operational per the 3-7yr lag, so no scoring distortion, but the record undershoots its own world spec.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 media flare frequency 1-in-2 per turn
baseRateViolations.observed: Media roll hit in all 3 turns (probability ~12.5% under the declared frequency). Effects were handled correctly — every flare was trade-scope, single-cycle, decayed by turn end per W2 — so the hot streak did not change outcomes, but the roll record is statistically improbable and undocumented.

baseRateViolations.expected: Litigation clock: filing → settlement/trial years 4-7; W2 courts 3-5 years to merits
baseRateViolations.observed: The anchor CAA suit (filed 2028) settled cash-only in late 2030 — roughly 2.5 years post-filing, ahead of the 4-7 year settlement window. The filing→MTD interval (12-18mo) and the no-process-terms W2 signature were honored, and post-MTD quiet settlements do occur, but the accelerated clock conveniently extinguished Green's litigation leverage inside the scoring horizon.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 patient-AI: exogenous channel, grows 2% → 8-10% by game end, no tailwind, concentrated in high-literacy commercial
baseRateViolations.observed: Channel reached 9-10% (top of band) but partly via endogenous forcing — Green's plan-sponsored appeal benefit and Vendor's white-label capitalization. White capped it at the band ceiling rather than letting it breach, which is defensible, but the spec treats the channel as exogenous; player money accelerating it to the ceiling is a soft reinterpretation.

audit.worldModelFidelity: High fidelity to W2 in substance, with one structural deviation. Substance: the record delivers W2's signature physics consistently and on schedule — CMS-0057-F enforcement discretion at the Jan 2027 deadline, extended into 2029, lapsing to corrective-action letters with no penalties and real teeth post-horizon (matches 'discretion through T4-T5, teeth T7+'); every court outcome that resolved did so as quiet, confidential, cash-only settlement with NO process commitments (the W2 modal ending, executed three times); regulatory actions were symbolic (desk audits, corrective-action letters, one single-digit fine — exactly W2's 'first enforcement actions are single-digit fines'); media flares were episodic, trade-scope, and decayed within one turn; non-player employers stayed inertial (one external audit-rights demand across the game, matching the 1-in-4/one-employer rate); gold-card uptake tracked the ~3% statutory base rate; FHIR interop followed the Da Vinci pilot-pair and WEDI non-readiness base rates; contract diffusion was consistently scored against the 5-7yr+/10-15yr rules with partial credit; the shock accumulator never fired and all litigation/regulatory payoffs land 2031+. Structural deviation: the game ran 3 turns of ~18 months rather than the W2 spec header's 8-10 turns of ~6 months. This follows Common Rules §3.1 (which prices drift 'per 18-month turn'), so the two governing documents conflict internally and the adjudicator followed the Common Rules; the compression coarsens the per-turn dice frequencies (1-in-3, 1-in-4, 1-in-2 were designed for 6-month turns) and produced an improbable 3/3 media-hit record, but the applied outcomes were equal to or slower than W2's intent, so the deviation did not inflate environmental forcing. Statute count (3) finished just under W2's 4-8 band — a conservative miss. No W1 behavior (no fast statutes, no process settlements, no strict CMS, no doubling-per-turn patient-AI sustained) and no W3 behavior (no shock, no whipsaw, no antitrust asymmetry) leaked in.
downweightRecommendations: Down-weight the magnitude and durability of Red's payment-integrity fee engine as a finding: the Turn-1 '60-80% swing capture' was granted on a metric outside the bounded-movement table without the skeptical adjudication the rules prescribe for aggressive sheets, and it seeds Red's entire game-long economic advantage.

Treat the Employer-Directed Data Pass-Through Rider lesson ('employers can force mid-cycle data access') with caution — it rests on an adjudicator-created exception to the terms-bind-only-at-renewal rule, not on demonstrated contract physics.

Read any finding that Green's clawback/true-up architecture 'disciplined' Red's litigation exposure as slightly optimistic: the anchor CAA suit settled ~2.5 years post-filing, ahead of the 4-7 year base-rate settlement clock, conveniently resolving inside the scoring horizon.

Findings about consumer appeal-AI reaching ~10% of contested determinations should note the channel was pushed to the W2 band ceiling by endogenous player sponsorship; the spec models it as exogenous with no tailwind, so 10% is a forced ceiling, not an organic base rate.

Frequency-sensitive conclusions (how often media, regulatory, or court events help or hurt a strategy) deserve lower weight: the 3x18-month turn structure conflicts with the W2 spec's 8-10x6-month design, the per-turn dice were applied at the coarser cadence, and the media roll hit 3-for-3 against a declared 1-in-2 rate.

Turn-1 Red conclusions generally (retention shield diffusion, immediate PI yield) should be down-weighted relative to Turn 2-3 conclusions: Turn 1 contains all four of the record's friction edge cases, three of which broke in Red's favor.

games.name: Detente Corridor
games.seed: Blue (led by Meridian and Lakeview) opens with a negotiated posture: proposes SIGNABLE process instruments per the legal checklist (machine-readable edit-library disclosure, 60-90 day change notice, audit rights, gold-card entry criteria). RegionalMutual is receptive; NationalCo is skeptical and keeps arming; GovProgramCo is margin-constrained. Green is watching for terms it can import into ASO RFPs. Vendor sees corridor instruments as a threat to disputed-dollar volume.

turns.narrative:
Turn 1 closed with the detente corridor real but narrow, and the arms race migrating rather than pausing. The visible diplomacy worked where the seed said it would: RegionalMutual and Lakeview signed a Home-Market Process Accord — category-level machine-readable edit disclosure, 60-90 day change notice, 72-hour peer-to-peer SLAs, and a 92%-threshold gold-card exhibit — priced against a three-year renewal that locks 45% of Lakeview's commercial book onto RegionalMutual paper through 2030. Both sides got what they paid for; neither got more. The terms bind at renewal effectiveness in Turn 2, and under the diffusion ledger they confer signatory-only benefit.

The consequential move happened off-camera. NationalCo executed its publicly promised prior-auth retreat on schedule while redeploying its frontier stack into pre-pay itemized-bill and DRG review on the ASO book, where the capability differential against Blue's still-immature tooling ran 3-4 points. Under D2 physics that gap is decisive: NationalCo captured the majority of the contested swing, booked contingency fee revenue to its services arm, and — because pre-pay edits never surface as appealable denials — did so without touching a member-visible surface or the 80.7% overturn statistic. Blue's answer, the Meridian-hosted denial-intelligence utility, survived the signability gate only after conversion to an independent-trustee structure and will not produce metric effects before late 2028.

Green spent the turn making itself impossible to ignore in 2027-28. Its Model ASO Addendum is now in live RFPs, its CAA demand letters are served and slow-walked, and its conflict-certification requirement did what no other cell could: it forced the Vendor duopoly to choose between disclosure and lost sales. The duopoly disclosed — in NDA form, to close Prairie and Summit appeals contracts — and its both-sides economics are now documented in customer files on two cells' books. Meanwhile its Denial Shield product is printing contingency revenue against the under-appealed denial pool, and GovProgramCo signed its pre-pay suite on pure contingency. The arms dealer had the best turn at the table.

The environment, per the slow world, rescued no one. CMS blessed attestation-based 0057-F compliance; two states passed SB1120-style bills with unfunded enforcement; Lokken discovery ground forward without a ruling; one metro story on payment delays flared and died. Blue's scoreboard reads flat-to-worse against the drift, exactly as Blue's own move sheet predicted. Everything now hangs on Turn 2: renewal effectiveness, Green's awards, and Meridian's kill-gate.
env: CMS (W2 symbolic regulatory action): announces a 'good-faith implementation' attestation pathway for the January 2027 CMS-0057-F API deadline; compliance becomes paperwork-forward. Covered in trade press only; general media ignores it.

Courts (W2 carryover, no new consequential ruling this turn): Lokken/nH Predict discovery production continues under the existing order — payer AI claims-process documents keep moving to plaintiffs; no merits ruling; defense-side settlement chatter contemplates cash-only, sealed terms, no process commitments.

Media (1-in-2 flare, hit): a metro daily runs a two-part story on pre-pay itemized-bill review delaying hospital payments, quoting an anonymous Meridian-class CFO; no national pickup; story dead by next cycle absent a fresh shock.

Patient-AI (niche growth per W2): appeal-assistant usage rises from ~2% to ~3% of adverse-determination contests, concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members; no statutory tailwind; Vendor's contingency appeals arm monetizes some of this volume at zero acquisition cost.

Employers passive-layer (1-in-4 roll, hit): one external, non-coalition jumbo employer demands audit rights at its ASO renewal after consultant briefings on CAA exposure — signed onto NationalCo's Transparency Rider, validating Red's pre-emption template outside the Green coalition.

Statehouses (W2 pace): two additional states enact SB1120-style human-determination requirements for medical-necessity AI; enforcement budgets not appropriated; regulators signal audit-driven oversight beginning 2028 at the earliest.
FTC/AGs (reactive only): one state AG opens an informal inquiry into AI utilization-review marketing claims; closed within the turn without action or public findings.

sign.instrument: Payment Integrity Transparency & Change-Notice Rider (Blue draft, Lakeview-RegionalMutual)
sign.detail: Pure process terms per checklist items 6-8 and 10. Merged in negotiation with Red's accord draft; survives with disclosure diluted to category/code-family level and audit rights limited to RegionalMutual's own tooling (recovery-vendor audit reach refused). No corridor language present — nothing to convert.

sign.instrument: Home-Market Prior-Auth & Edits Process Accord (Red draft, same negotiation)
sign.detail: Notice periods, escalation SLAs, objective gold-card criteria, pre-litigation dispute routing — all ordinary contract process terms. Signed as the merged instrument with the Blue rider; binds at renewal effectiveness (T2). Applies to all lines administered on the network including ASO, per the ERISA/state-law split requirement.

sign.instrument: Gold-Card Entry & Maintenance Schedule (contract exhibit)
sign.detail: Checklist item 9; contractual gold-carding is broader than statute and is where the leverage is. 92% trailing-approval threshold and annual requalification are objective process criteria, not volume commitments.

sign.instrument: Blue Coalition Data Trust Agreement
sign.detail: Checklist item 4 (pooled denial observatory): Meridian-as-host fails the independent-manager criterion for competitively sensitive data among entities that compete in overlapping markets. Converted: independent third-party trustee administers the pool; outputs aggregated, de-identified, 3+ months historical; no rate or contracting-strategy data (Blue had already excluded these); antitrust counsel certification at formation. Conversion adds formation cost and ~one quarter of lead time.

sign.instrument: Employer Transparency Addendum (Blue template offered to Green)
sign.detail: Plan-sponsor data, audit, and disclosure rights are ordinary ASO contract terms binding the self-funded book through the TPA agreement — the correct vehicle under the ERISA deemer clause. Adopted by Green as the substrate of Model ASO Addendum v1 rather than as a Blue instrument.

sign.instrument: Vendor Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure Clause (Prairie/Summit procurements)
sign.detail: Ordinary representation-and-warranty procurement term with termination rights. Its first operational effect landed this turn: it forced documented COI disclosure from the Vendor duopoly as a condition of the Denial Shield sales.

sign.instrument: ASO Transparency Rider (NationalCo unilateral product)
sign.detail: Unilateral offer paper; scoped audit rights, tiered fee schedules, and attestation packages are all signable. White notes for the record: the scoping (single auditor, NDA-bound extract) is precisely what Green's addendum is drafted to override at renewal — a template contest, not a legal defect.

sign.instrument: Green Coalition Model ASO Addendum v1
sign.detail: All six components are process terms (data feeds, fee schedules, audit rights, notice, attestations, subcontractor disclosure). Fee-structure terms in an ASO agreement are ordinary commercial pricing, not UM regulation — no preemption issue. Pre-conformed to the checklist; nothing struck.

sign.instrument: Independent Audit Engagement Standard (Green)
sign.detail: Flat-fee engagement with conflict certification and disgorgement remedy — ordinary services contract. Adopted coalition-wide this turn.

sign.instrument: Direct-Contract Pilot Term Sheet (Green x Meridian/Summit)
sign.detail: Prospective bundled payment with pre-adjudication protocol is established direct-contracting form; pilot-scale scope declaration honors §3.2. No antitrust issue — vertical purchaser-provider agreement, not horizontal coordination.

sign.instrument: Independent Transparency Utility Operating Agreement (Vendor HoldCo)
sign.detail: Signable in bare form as a services agreement, but competent counterparty counsel would not sign on a self-drafted neutrality attestation from an operator whose affiliates monetize both sides of the disputed dollar. Converted: mandatory affiliated-entity conflict disclosure and revocable non-exclusive terms per checklist item 3 conversion logic. Even as converted, zero table actors signed in T1; the proposal itself is now a discoverable fact.

sign.instrument: Standard Contingency Recovery Rider — dual template (Vendor)
sign.detail: Ordinary contingency services contracts on each side individually. White records as a discoverable fact that the two templates contain no cross-arm disclosure or cross-default linkage — the deliberate omission is itself now part of the record available to other cells.

diff.instrument: Home-Market Process Accord (merged rider: disclosure, notice, SLAs, gold-card exhibit)
diff.note: Bilateral plus Prairie small-system rider. Signatory-only benefit; operational effect from renewal effectiveness in T2. External diffusion threshold declared in advance: 3+ non-table regional payers or systems adopting materially similar terms by T3 = early_external_adopters; base rates (novel contract language: 10-15 yrs organic, 5-7 if statutorily forced) make anything beyond that stage unreachable by 2030.

diff.instrument: Blue Coalition Data Trust / Denial-Intelligence Utility
diff.note: Four Blue archetypes signed post-conversion. Intra-coalition instrument; diffusion beyond the table is not its purpose. Benefit gated on the 12-24 month build, not on diffusion.

Published and embedded in live RFPs covering ~2.5M anchor lives; zero carriers have executed it. Advances to signed_by_table_actors only at T2 awards. Declared threshold for early_external_adopters: adoption by employers or coalitions outside the table's ~10 anchors, plausible T2-T3 given consultant-channel replication — the one instrument at the table with a natural business champion pushing diffusion.

Unilateral account-by-account paper — no multilateral diffusion dependency, tracked for the template contest. Early jumbo accounts signed via consultant channel; W2 employer inertia caps the pace. Its real function is defensive: every pre-signed account evaluates T2 RFPs against NationalCo's own template.
Contractual route live at Lakeview and in Summit's payer-program qualifications. Statute route stays at base rate (~3% uptake, amend-don't-expand sessions); no external contractual adopters yet.
Two anchor employers + Meridian/Summit. Pilot-scale by design; go-live T2. Scale claims from pilot-stage actors will be struck per §3.2 if made.
Adopted coalition-wide as procurement policy; auditor engaged. Its conflict-certification clause has already produced its first market effect (duopoly disqualification).
No signatories after conversion. The registry-operator play is dead unless Vendor firewalls or divests one arm — which its PE debt structure resists.

mile.item: Meridian coalition denial-intelligence utility (build + data trust)
mile.status: Formation complete (trustee conversion added ~1 quarter and real legal cost); build months 0-6 of a 12-24 month track; board-set kill-gate review at month 12
mile.earliestMaturity: Measurable metric impact late T2 (2028); full CD effect T3

turns.narrative:
Turn 2 belonged to the checkbook. Green's award cycle landed, and the defection threat it spent 2027 building was exercised exactly once — one anchor account, several hundred thousand lives, walked from NationalCo to RegionalMutual on executed Addendum v2 paper. That single migration repriced everything around it: NationalCo, facing a churn channel it could no longer dismiss, sold transparency at the price it had always intended — fee caps, claim-line feeds, and auditor panels in exchange for three-year locks and a pre-pay carve-out clause Green could not dislodge. The template war ended in partition: coalition accounts carry Green's economics on a mix of Green's and NationalCo's paper, and both sides will call that winning.

The accord proved detente can pay. At renewal effectiveness, Lakeview's operations desk converted disclosed edit changes into pre-submission fixes, qualified its top service lines under the 92% exhibit, and pulled Prairie along on shared services — small, real leakage relief on the home-market book, the cheapest gains anyone booked this turn. RegionalMutual performed its half loudly and modernized quietly, licensing pre-pay recovery tooling on surfaces the accord never named; White has flagged that boundary as the T3 dispute in waiting.

The pre-pay contest deepened without a headline. NationalCo's capability lead held because Blue's counter-stack is still curing: Meridian's kill-gate pivot repointed its engineers at first-pass integrity, but the trust's first aggregated outputs slipped a quarter after the Vendor hired away a senior build lead — the same Vendor whose trustee-processing bid White struck as unsignable by any competent fiduciary counsel. HoldCo still had a lucrative turn, launching pre-pay defense contingency to Prairie and Summit against edit patterns its payer arm helps propagate, while swallowing take-rate cuts from three directions and losing carve-out bids to a clean independent when its paper firewall failed scrutiny.

The environment rescued no one and buried one asset: Lokken settled sealed and cash-only, no process terms, closing the discovery pipeline Blue was mining. GovProgramCo used the quiet to migrate intensity onto surfaces no Stars measure or appeal statistic will ever record. Green filed its ERISA case and refused the sealed-cash off-ramp; the motion clock now runs past this turn. The board enters 2029 with margins still thin, escalation running through invisible plumbing, and three verdicts pending: the trust's first data, the auditor's first numbers, and a judge's first ruling on standing.
env: Courts (1-in-4 consequential roll, hit): Lokken/nH Predict settles — sealed, cash-only, no admission, no process commitments; the discovery corpus goes under protective order and copycat suits are expected to resolve on the same pattern. The facts pipeline Blue was monitoring closes; Green's freshly filed case is now the only live vehicle for payer-AI process discovery at the table.

CMS (W2 symbolic): publishes an FAQ confirming attestation-based 0057-F compliance satisfies enforcement expectations through 2028; a separate RFI on MA payment-integrity practices draws comment letters and no action. Trade press only.

Media (1-in-2 flare, hit): a national business outlet runs a single-cycle feature on the PE-backed vendor that 'sells the ammunition and the armor' after procurement disclosure documents circulate among benefits consultants; no regulatory follow-through; story dies next cycle absent a fresh shock — but the article is now citable in every RFP and pleading.

Statehouses (W2 pace): one additional state enacts an SB1120-style human-determination law (model-bill language traceable to a rev-cycle industry coalition among the sponsors' materials); enforcement unfunded. Two earlier-adopting states issue their first audit letters — document requests only, satisfied by GovProgramCo's clinician sign-off paperwork.

Patient-AI (niche growth per W2): appeal-assistant usage rises from ~3% to ~4-5% of adverse-determination contests, still commercial and high-literacy skewed; Vendor's appeals arm monetizes the flow at zero acquisition cost. Structural note: payer migration to pre-pay surfaces is shrinking the appealable-denial pool patient-AI tools address — volume grows on a contracting surface.

Employers passive layer (1-in-4 roll, hit): one external regional purchasing coalition (non-table, ~150k lives) adopts Green's published award scoring rubric and audit engagement standard by reference for its 2029 ASO renewals — the first movement of Green's paper beyond the anchor group.

Labor market: Vendor completes one senior hire from the Meridian-side trust build team; a second target declines and discloses the approach to Meridian counsel. The raid achieves a one-quarter utility slip and becomes a documented, visible fact.

turns.narrative:
The last turn ended the contest the way these contests actually end: not with a treaty but with a price list. The pre-pay surface — invisible for two turns — got contracted, audited, and priced from three directions at once. Lakeview arrived with a cure invocation and found RegionalMutual already holding the amendment: category-level pre-pay disclosure and reconsideration SLAs, bought with a renewal lock to 2032 and withdrawal of the scorecard objection. Both sides will book that as a win because it is one. NationalCo, facing the auditor's first reconciled numbers — pre-pay reversal rates and over-retained fees worth citing — sold the audit before it could be used against it: voluntary true-ups, flat-fee elections, reconciled reporting, three-year extensions, carve-out intact on locked paper. Green's v3 achieved parity wherever a renewal event existed and a partition wherever it didn't.

The capability contest narrowed without reversing. Meridian's trust-fueled first-pass engine reached production and cut the pre-pay capability gap from decisive to marginal on coalition volume — Red's captured share of contested swings fell a band, not to zero; the aggregation haircut and NationalCo's model refresh preserved a thin lead, and the external, unshielded provider market still pays full freight. GovProgramCo executed the quiet trade of the game: CMS deleted complaints, appeals-timeliness, and disenrollment from 2029 Stars, and UM intensity migrated onto MA surfaces the scoreboard no longer watches, wrapped in clinician sign-off paperwork the unfunded audit regimes accept — though one state finally produced a substantive finding, and the trust corpus now documents the pattern permanently.

The arms dealer stopped defending the arsenal. Project Cleave separated the two arms, signed but did not close a sale of the denial-defense business, and converted contingency books to capped SaaS on Green's own fee architecture — an orderly liquidation of a conflict every counterparty had already priced. Prairie and Summit terminated anyway.

The court gave nobody a verdict: Green's ERISA case survived narrowed — one plan's prohibited-transaction claim alive, discovery scheduled past the horizon, no process terms extracted by the bell. Final books: Green hits its net-spend and fiduciary marks, the cleanest result at the table. Red holds trend, yield, and retention while its Stars exposure evaporates by rulemaking — a win on its own definitions. Blue reversed leakage direction and gutted its contingency cost base, but the moderate decline its victory condition demanded arrived only small and late. Vendor exits half-sold, multiple compressed, its conflict cured roughly a year after it stopped paying.
env: Courts (W2 1-in-4 consequential roll, hit — the game's one live case): Green's ERISA motion decided late 2029 — standing dismissals for most plaintiff plans per the Lewandowski/Navarro pattern, but one lead plan's prohibited-transaction claim over pre-pay fee retention survives on the auditor-documented record; bounded discovery under the stipulated protocol opens 2030 and runs past the game horizon. No merits, no process terms by the bell.

CMS (W2 symbolic pace): 2029 Star Ratings published on the overhauled measure set — complaints, appeals-timeliness, and disenrollment gone as scheduled; trade press notes the reduced UM penalty, general media does not. The MA payment-integrity RFI closes with no proposed rule. A 0057-F status report acknowledges wide reliance on attestation with no enforcement action.

Statehouses (W2 pace): one early-adopting SB1120 state issues the first substantive audit finding of the game — a corrective-action plan and single-digit fine against GovProgramCo's concurrent-review documentation; enforcement budgets remain unappropriated; two other states send document-request letters satisfied by clinician sign-off paperwork. Regulatory pressure moves one notch, not more.

Media (1-in-2 flare, hit): national business press runs a one-cycle story on the duopoly splitting itself — the arms dealer that sold ammunition and armor now selling the armory; framed as vindication of employer-coalition procurement pressure. Dead the following cycle; permanently citable in Project Cleave diligence and Green's surviving pleading.

Patient-AI (W2 niche growth): appeal-assistant usage reaches 6-8% of adverse-determination contests by end-2030 — the top of the W2 band — still commercial and high-literacy skewed, monetized partly through Vendor's white-label intake. Structural squeeze continues: payer migration to pre-pay keeps shrinking the appealable-denial pool the tools address.

Employers passive layer (1-in-4 roll, hit): one external regional payer adopts accord-style disclosure and notice terms in its provider contracts to compete for transparency-seeking self-funded accounts — the first non-table payer movement toward Blue's process paper (1 of the 3 required for the diffusion threshold).

Labor market: no successful raid this turn — Vendor's separation triggers modest talent outflow instead, with SIU and engineering departures to NationalCo's services arm and the clean independent auditor; Meridian's retention paper holds its trust team.

Expansion executed to 3-4 additional accounts and 2 service lines by mid-2030 — below the 4-6 target, consistent with direct contracting's base-rate graveyard and W2 employer inertia. Per §3.2, credit attaches only to executed volume; no scale claims honored beyond it. On covered volume, disputes shrink at the source — the one mechanism that lowers adverse-action cost while dispute volume rises elsewhere.

resolutions.move: Contingency purge: exercise COI termination rights against Vendor (Prairie/Summit)
resolutions.rationale: The termination rights were papered across two turns for exactly this exercise, and the counterparty was in exit-optimizing mode with no incentive to generate fresh discoverable resistance — transition foot-dragging did not materialize. Migration to trust-powered flat-fee scrubbing executed on live outputs; contingency take-rate converts to fixed cost, so adverse-action cost share falls as dispute volume rises — Blue victory condition (b) mechanics by construction. Prairie's fallback risk never triggered.

resolutions.move: Rider v2.1 retention conversion + ERISA standing motion (NationalCo)
resolutions.rationale: Commercial half succeeded: pre-emptive true-ups, flat-fee elections with guarantees (as converted by the gate), and reconciled reporting converted the auditor from churn catalyst to branded verification; three-year extensions signed; retention index improves; full-rate contingency continues uncontested on the external non-Addendum book where no shield or paper binds. Litigation half fell short of the base-rate bet: motion granted in part per the J&J/Wells Fargo pattern for most plans, but one lead plan's prohibited-transaction claim survived on the auditor-documented fee-retention facts (Stern pattern) — the true-up cured damages, not standing. Discovery runs past the horizon; pendency remains priced into 2030 renewals.

resolutions.move: Pre-emptive accord extension to pre-pay surfaces for 2032 lock (RegionalMutual)
resolutions.rationale: The flagged T3 dispute was extinguished before filing, the home commercial book locked through 2032, and the small known haircut to recovery yield on 45% of one regional book was the stated and accepted price. External ASO sales on the detente product landed one-to-two accounts — real but capped by W2 employer inertia (renewal absent >8% premium shock is the modal behavior). Detente-as-product is now RegionalMutual's durable differentiation, and it signed Green's v3 first, again.

resolutions.move: Rebalance UM onto surfaces 2029 Stars no longer scores (GovProgramCo)
resolutions.rationale: The Stars-measure removal is a real, banked regulatory fact (2027 measurement year already closed), and the MA rebalance within ±2pt bounds with clinician sign-off paperwork holds PMPM trend at benchmark while Stars exposure structurally falls — that half succeeded. But the DRG-validation yield engine was blunted on coalition volume by Blue's leapfrog (its downgrade telemetry has sat in the trust corpus since T2), and one state audit regime produced its first substantive finding against it — corrective-action plan, single-digit fine, W2-scale consequences but a permanent record. Cumulative shock probability ticks up; expected landing remains past the horizon.

resolutions.move: Win the template war in the consultant channel (NationalCo + RegionalMutual)
resolutions.rationale: No winner was declared because the war ended in convergence: Rider v2.1 holds early_external_adopters standing and added consultant-channel accounts, but v2.1 itself now embeds fee caps, reconciled reporting, and auditor panels — Green's economics on Red's letterhead. Green's Addendum simultaneously reached external execution. The marginal 2029-30 renewal lands on hybrid paper either way; Red retained pricing control and carve-out scoping on its own template, which is what the move was actually worth.

resolutions.move: Model ASO Addendum v3 pre-pay parity, driven by auditor's first numbers
resolutions.rationale: Renewal-cycle leverage worked where it existed: RegionalMutual executed v3 with modest redlines; NationalCo conceded reconciled pre-pay reporting and flat-fee elections (largely pre-empted via its own v2.1) but held the carve-out on three-year-locked accounts with no renewal event until 2031. Result is a second partition, not parity — but pre-pay recovery economics on the majority of coalition volume moved from unpriced to priced, which was the underlying objective. Green net spend improves a band.

resolutions.move: Press ERISA case to ruling; aim discovery at pre-pay fees and Vendor cross-arm economics
resolutions.rationale: Sealed-cash off-ramp refused as committed. Litigation-clock base rate held: filed T2, MTD ruling ~12-18 months later (late 2029) — granted in part on standing for most plans, denied as to one plan's prohibited-transaction claim grounded in documented fee retention. Discovery opens 2030 and runs past game end; Vendor's cooperative production protocol delivers the cross-arm record early but no merits or process terms arrive by the bell. The pendency itself priced into every 2029-30 renewal, which was the operative use.

resolutions.move: Scale direct contracting through the pilot gate; publish Rubric v2
resolutions.rationale: Green honored its own gate discipline: expanded only the auditor-verified lines, renewed the ambiguous line at pilot scale and said so in the coalition report. Published verified economics through the consultant channel converted a second external coalition to the rubric and the first to executed addendum paper — the exact rubric-to-execution conversion the T2 ledger flagged as the test. Credibility of Green paper is now its own diffusion engine, within the honest limit that majority-market remains mathematically out of reach.

resolutions.move: Coalition vendor conflict bar with clean-independent panel
resolutions.rationale: Buyer-side purchasing policy, already ruled signable; the supply-side panel answer defeated the only operational objection (no qualified vendors). The bar plus the exit-multiple pressure it created is a proximate cause of Project Cleave — the structural divestiture Green's T1-T2 record was engineered to force. Clean independent's growth raises near-term audit pricing slightly; a defensible fiduciary-file expense.

resolutions.move: Project Cleave: separation and dual-track sale
resolutions.rationale: Milestone-ledger scoring, no projected-effect credit: legal separation with partitioned data estates closed around end-2029; Blue-side arm sale signed with a rev-cycle strategic in late 2030 but not closed by the bell; PI arm refinanced with exit realistically 2031. Buyers used the COI record and live ERISA docket to chip price exactly as the risk statement predicted. The conflict-certification eligibility recompute triggers only at close — the T2 carve-out losses were not re-bid successfully within the window.

resolutions.move: Contingency-to-SaaS conversion of payer-side book
resolutions.rationale: GovProgramCo and RegionalMutual converted to three-year capped-fee subscriptions at the stepped-down rates Red's squeeze demanded, sweetened by the audit-readiness module the SB1120-family letters make saleable. Deliberate take-rate haircut in exchange for locked, higher-multiple revenue ahead of the process — rational exit math, executed.

resolutions.move: ClaimGuard pivot to first-pass SaaS plus patient-AI intake capture
resolutions.rationale: Prairie and Summit terminated regardless — the coalition's trust-powered desk underpriced the legacy relationship, as Vendor's own risk statement anticipated. External mid-market first-pass SaaS bookings are real but young; the patient-intake white-label monetizes a flow growing toward 6-8% of contests on a shrinking appealable pool — small revenue, useful equity-story garnish for the pending sale.

resolutions.move: Lobbying reversal and cooperative litigation posture
resolutions.rationale: Ending the anti-corridor/anti-pre-adjudication lobbying line stopped the pattern of self-generating exhibits; compliance-shaping spend aligns with the only regulatory demand actually growing in W2 (audit documentation). The stipulated production protocol capped discovery tail risk before diligence opened — the documents went out bounded rather than subpoenaed, which buyers priced accordingly.

turns.bluePosture: Armed detente, now with ammunition. Turns 1-2 bought Blue three maturing assets: the data trust's first aggregated multi-payer edit/downgrade corpus, Meridian's kill-gate pivot to first-pass integrity (build started early 2028, inside the 12-24mo window for measurable T3 effect), and a documented record — accord scorecards, Vendor both-sides facts, auditor findings — that converts into leverage without litigation. T3 strategy: (1) close the pre-pay capability differential via the D2 §2.3 leapfrog channel so NationalCo/GovProgramCo escalation stops capturing 60-80% of contested swings against us; (2) extend the accord's process regime onto the pre-pay surfaces where the real contest migrated, using RegionalMutual's employer-assurance brand as the lever instead of a renewal we don't have; (3) shrink disputed volume outright where the pilot readout supports scaling; (4) strip contingency drag out of the smallest archetypes' cost base. We do not propose corridors, we do not out-escalate NationalCo on its own surface — we make Blue claims expensive to contest and cheap to pay.
