cellAssessments.blue: Third place, and a study in disciplined asymmetry. Blue correctly diagnosed at Turn 1 that it would lose a symmetric capability contest on ASO volume and never wavered from that read: it traded process terms for stability where the counterparty was receptive (Lakeview-RegionalMutual accord), pooled data through the trustee-converted trust to close the capability gap prospectively, and outsourced its offense to Green's checkbook by handing over documented facts. The kill-gate pivot from appeals automation to first-pass integrity was the right call made on time. But Blue's assets all matured late — the trust slipped a quarter to a talent raid, production arrived mid-2029, and the capability gap closed from decisive (3-4) to marginal (1-2), never to zero. It met its cost and margin conditions but missed its leakage-decline target (small, not moderate). Verdict: strategically correct, temporally short — one more turn and its position compounds.
cellAssessments.red: Second place, winning on its own definitions throughout. Red's two-surface strategy — perform transparency loudly where scored (employer retention, home market, Stars), press the capability lead where invisible (pre-pay ASO review) — worked for three consecutive turns. NationalCo's Turn 1 migration from prior auth to pre-pay was the single best move at the table: it honored the public pledge while relocating the disputed dollar to a surface with no appealable denials, no overturn statistic, and no member-visible churn trigger. Critically, Red was never cost-constrained: its self-funded PI engine stayed fee-revenue-positive to the bell, and every concession it made (fee caps, true-ups, reconciled reporting, the 2032 lock) was proximately purchased by employer defection risk, auditor numbers, or litigation pendency — and always sold at a price of Red's choosing, with the pre-pay carve-out defended on locked paper. The 2029 Stars overhaul then deleted its residual member-visible exposure by rulemaking. Red ended with trend flat, yield improving, retention improving.
cellAssessments.green: First place and the game's structural winner. Green never fired a shot in the capability war; it repriced both arsenals. The sequence was textbook: Turn 1 built the instruments (Model Addendum, conflict-certification clause, demand letters, direct-contract paper); Turn 2 cashed them at award season — one anchor-account defection was enough to convert NationalCo from dismissal to negotiation; Turn 3 dragged the pre-pay surface into the same disclosure/fee-cap/carve-out regime using the auditor's first reconciled numbers. Its conflict-certification standard restructured the vendor market (two carve-out wins for the clean independent, proximate causation of Project Cleave), and its rubric was the only paper at the table to clear the external-diffusion threshold by 2030. Ended with net spend improving moderately, fiduciary exposure low, and the only live discovery vehicle into payer-AI economics. The purchaser, independently modeled, proved to be the binding constraint the regulator never was.
cellAssessments.vendor: Fourth place after the best opening turn at the table. The both-sides model printed ARR through 2027-28 — Denial Shield on Blue volume, pre-pay suites on Red volume, contingency on patient-AI flow at zero acquisition cost — but every sale under a conflict-certification regime deposited discoverable evidence in someone else's files. The transparency-utility capture play died twice (zero signatories, then the trustee processing bid struck at the gate), the talent raid bought one quarter of delay at the price of a documented pattern, and by 2029 the conflict was a multiple compressor: cited in a national feature, a live ERISA pleading, and every RFP. Project Cleave was the rational endgame — monetize the dissolution, convert contingency to capped SaaS on Green's own fee architecture — but it closed roughly a year after the conflict stopped paying: Blue-arm sale signed but unclosed at the bell, PI arm refinanced and unsold, Prairie and Summit terminated anyway. The arms dealer thesis worked until the ammunition became evidence.

criticalJunctures: Turn 1: NationalCo executes its promised prior-auth retreat while redeploying its frontier stack into pre-pay itemized-bill/DRG review on the ASO book — the escalation migrates to a surface that generates no appealable denials, no overturn statistic, and no member-visible trigger, setting the entire game's terrain.

Turn 1: White Cell converts the Blue data trust to an independent-trustee structure and Green's conflict-certification clause forces the Vendor duopoly into documented COI disclosure — two gate rulings that later lock Vendor out of the transparency plumbing and arm the 2029 endgame.

Turn 2: Green's award cycle produces exactly one anchor-account defection (several hundred thousand lives from NationalCo to RegionalMutual on Addendum v2 paper) — the single event that made the churn threshold credible and converted NationalCo from resisting transparency to pricing it.

Turn 2: Meridian's kill-gate is exercised as a pivot (appeals automation to first-pass integrity) rather than a kill — preserving Blue's only capability-gap-closing asset; the simultaneous Vendor talent raid costs it one quarter, nearly enough to matter.

Turn 2: Lokken settles sealed and cash-only, closing the discovery pipeline; Green refuses the same off-ramp and files, making its ERISA case the only live vehicle for payer-AI process discovery for the rest of the game.

Turn 3: The independent auditor's first reconciled numbers (pre-pay reversal rates, over-retained fees) land — NationalCo sells the audit before it can be used against it (true-ups, flat-fee elections, reconciled reporting), and RegionalMutual pre-empts the accord boundary dispute by voluntarily extending disclosure to pre-pay surfaces for a 2032 lock.

Turn 3 environment: CMS's 2029 Stars overhaul removes complaints/appeals/disenrollment measures as scheduled — the deregulatory rulemaking that lets GovProgramCo rebalance UM intensity onto surfaces no scoreboard watches, the game's quietest decisive event.

Turn 3: Project Cleave — the Vendor duopoly separates its arms under procurement pressure rather than regulatory compulsion, an orderly liquidation of a conflict every counterparty had already priced.
rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By end-2030 the conflict has neither burned out nor been settled by treaty; it has been priced. The adversarial contest over the disputed healthcare dollar migrated twice — first out of prior authorization (retired publicly, on schedule, as cover) into pre-pay claim review on self-funded volume, where payer capability advantages were largest and nothing was visible to members, statistics, or regulators; then, in the final eighteen months, that invisible surface itself was dragged under contract: disclosed at category level, fee-capped, audited by conflict-certified independents, subject to reconsideration SLAs, and reconciled against plan assets. The mechanism that accomplished this was not government — the slow-world regulator spent five years issuing attestation pathways, unfunded statutes, and one single-digit fine — but the purchaser: employer fiduciaries converted CAA duty into procurement leverage, demonstrated a credible defection channel exactly once, and thereafter sold retention to carriers at the price of transparency. The end-state is a lattice of bilateral, renewal-priced process instruments (edit-library disclosure, change notice, gold-card and clean-claim certification exhibits, fee reconciliation, carve-out rights) laid over a capability contest that continues at reduced amplitude: the payer capability lead narrowed from decisive to marginal on coalition volume but persists, unshielded providers outside the coalitions still pay full freight, and utilization-management intensity has rebalanced onto Medicare Advantage surfaces that the 2029 ratings overhaul stopped scoring. The both-sides vendor that tolled the conflict was forced by procurement paper — not regulation — to dismember itself. Nothing converged to a market norm: every binding instrument is signatory-level, external diffusion reached only early adopters, and the one live lawsuit will produce its first public fee record after the horizon. It is an equilibrium of documented, audited, contractually-metered adversarialism — cheaper per disputed dollar, vastly better recorded, and stable only until the 2031 renewal wave reprices the carve-outs that survived.
rapporteur.excursionSummary: GAME B1G2 (D2 escalation-viable doctrine, W2 slow world, GREEN and VENDOR cells active) opened on a negotiated Blue posture and ended, per the closing adjudication, "not with a treaty but with a price list." The defining dynamic was surface migration under visibility arbitrage: NationalCo's Turn 1 prior-auth retreat was executed as promised and simultaneously hollowed out, with its frontier stack redeployed to pre-pay itemized-bill/DRG review on ASO volume — a 3-4 point capability differential on a surface producing no appealable denials and no member-visible events. Under D2 physics that captured the majority of contested swing for two turns. Blue declined symmetric escalation, holding the Lakeview-RegionalMutual process accord (the game's durable detente kernel, extended to pre-pay surfaces by 2030 for a 2032 lock) while building a trustee-administered data pool that cut the capability gap to 1-2 points by production in mid-2029 — late enough that Blue missed its leakage target and finished third. The decisive force was Green. The employer cell converted CAA fiduciary duty into procurement leverage, and one anchor-account defection at the 2028 awards repriced NationalCo's entire posture: fee caps, claim-line feeds, auditor panels, then true-ups and flat-fee elections once the independent auditor's reconciled pre-pay numbers landed in 2029. Red conceded transparency repeatedly but never from cost pain — its self-funded PI engine stayed fee-positive throughout, and every concession was proximately triggered by employer abrasion, auditor documentation, or litigation pendency, always exchanged for term locks. GovProgramCo executed the quiet trade of the game, migrating UM intensity onto MA surfaces the 2029 Stars overhaul stopped scoring. The Vendor duopoly had the best opening turn (arming both sides, tolling the conflict) and the worst endgame: Green's conflict-certification standard progressively documented its both-sides economics into procurement files, a national feature story, and a surviving ERISA pleading, compressing its exit multiple until Project Cleave — self-dismemberment under procurement pressure — became the rational close. The regulator mattered almost entirely through inaction: attestation-based 0057-F compliance, unfunded SB1120 statutes, a sealed Lokken settlement, and a deregulatory Stars rulemaking that enabled rather than constrained. Final ordinal: Green, Red, Blue, Vendor. Every binding instrument in the game was a process or pricing term; no numeric denial-rate corridor was ever proposed, let alone signed; and no instrument diffused beyond early external adopters by the bell. Escalation ended moderate and contractually metered, not extinguished.
keyDynamics: Visibility arbitrage as the escalation mode: adverse-action intensity migrated from appealable, member-visible denial surfaces (prior auth) to non-appealable pre-pay edits and, later, to MA surfaces removed from Stars scoring — escalation persisted by relocating to wherever no scoreboard watched.

The purchaser, not the regulator, was the binding constraint: in a slow world, employer fiduciary/procurement mechanics (one demonstrated defection, fee caps, conflict certification, independent audit) moved payer behavior years before any statute, court, or agency did.

Process terms as the universal signable currency: every executed instrument across all three turns was process or commercial pricing paper; numeric denial-rate corridors never even reached a gate ruling because no actor proposed one.

Capability-differential economics governed the contest: pooled data (the coalition trust) was Blue's only gap-closing channel, and the 12-24 month build clock meant the gap narrowed from decisive to marginal but never reversed inside the horizon — timing, not strategy, set Blue's ceiling.

Documented facts as slow-fuse ammunition: gate strikes, COI disclosures, scorecards, and auditor numbers accumulated as discoverable records that detonated one to three turns later through procurement and litigation channels, never through regulators.

Conflict-of-interest certification as a market-structuring instrument: a single procurement rep-and-warranty clause disqualified the vendor duopoly twice, redirected carve-out awards to a clean independent, and proximately caused the duopoly's self-separation.

Concessions were always sold, never surrendered: every Red transparency concession was exchanged for term locks and retention, keeping Red's book intact — de-escalation was priced as a product, not accepted as defeat.

registryScores.evidence: No formal denial constraint (statute, corridor, or White ruling) bound in this game, so the displacement ratio is not computable from the ledger. But the qualitative mechanism replicated exactly: NationalCo's publicly pledged prior-auth retreat (T1) was accompanied by immediate redeployment into pre-pay itemized-bill/DRG review on ASO volume — recovery migrating to channels that 'never surface as appealable denials' — and GovProgramCo later migrated intensity onto post-Stars-overhaul MA surfaces. Channel displacement under constraint of the visible surface was total and fast; the >=0.33 dollar ratio cannot be certified in this cell.

The W2 channel-shift rider held for adversarial artifacts: Vendor's transparency-utility proposal, dual contingency templates, and struck trustee bid all became discoverable facts cited in Green's ERISA pleading, Project Cleave diligence, and a national feature — media/negotiation/litigation channels, ~2-3 turn lags, no regulator involved. NationalCo's published Aggregate PI Transparency Report was flagged citable against it in the surviving claim. However, Green's published artifacts (rubric, audit benchmark) were net-positive with zero adverse citation, and Blue's accord scorecards paid off (cure invocation leverage) — so the claim that <50% of artifacts stay cost-free is not supported for purchaser-side publishers in this game.

The game record contains no per-turn cost-per-denial ledger or dollar figures; state variables are qualitative bands only. Directionally consistent facts exist — trustee conversion added formation cost, audit/attestation/arbitration tolls recurred every turn, and Blue's cost relief came from purging contingency drag rather than tolls disappearing — but neither the $65/$80 floor nor the volume-cost correlation can be computed.

Core D2xW2 test, cleanly passed. Red's self-funded PI activity stayed fee-revenue-positive all three turns (redPIYield improving in every turn's state block); Red never initiated de-escalation from cost. Every Red concession was proximately triggered by external channels: the T2 fee-cap/transparency sale followed the anchor-account defection (employer channel); T3 true-ups and reconciled reporting followed the auditor's numbers and ERISA pendency (employer + litigation); RegionalMutual's pre-pay extension purchased a renewal lock (employer/commercial). Zero cost-exhaustion triggers coded.

The corridor half is fully supported in this cell: every signed instrument across three turns was a process or pricing term (White's gate log: 'nothing approaches a corridor' repeatedly); no numeric denial-rate corridor was proposed or signed. The end-state half is directionally supported for D2: this game did not converge to comprehensive detente — the accord remained bilateral/signatory-only while escalation continued on migrated surfaces — but a single game cannot establish the <33% F2-primary rate across D2/D3 cells.

No actor published an AI-governance charter; the publisher-vs-internal-governor pairing never formed. Weakly consistent observation: GovProgramCo governed internally (SB1120 clinician sign-off wrappers, gated publication) and suffered only one single-digit fine in five years, but with no publisher comparator the 2x adverse-event ratio is untestable.

Zero distress events of any tier occurred — no distress sale, PE acquisition, or exclusivity-delegation capture at any actor. Prairie (rural-small) survived via accord riders and shared-services subscriptions; mid-tier archetypes held via coalition pooling. The absence is mildly adverse to the 'modal structural casualty' claim but this cell featured an unusually effective Blue coalition; tier-rate comparisons require the cross-cell pool.

Rolling distribution and wedge-first: supported — binding instruments spread across 2027 (accord signing), 2028 (renewal effectiveness, Addendum v2 awards, Rider v2), and 2029-30 (pre-pay extension, v3, v2.1, SaaS riders); first-cycle wins were pure process wedges with full fee economics arriving only in cycle two-plus. The D2 late-peak sub-claim failed in this game: the escalation index ran elevated in T1-T2 and declined to moderate in the final turn — escalation was priced down into 2030, not peaking there.

One D2xW2 data point, and it points toward the refute (inside-view) direction: despite escalation-viable doctrine and a regulator that delivered nothing but attestations and unfunded statutes, the game did not end in grinding uncoordinated escalation — agents found the off-ramp the doctrine did not remove (the employer checkbook), and escalation ended moderate under bilateral price-list instruments. The >=40% F1-primary frequency claim requires the full cell; this game contributes a non-F1 outcome to that denominator.

Robust strategies that were run paid: renewal loading (accord terms priced into Lakeview and 2032 locks), prevention-over-appeals (kill-gate pivot to first-pass integrity reversed Blue's leakage direction), upcoding inoculation analog (clean-claim certification executed), BATNA-first (Green's direct-contract pilot cleared its gate and anchored award leverage). Fragile-set confirmation: Vendor's anti-corridor lobbying and weaponized-neutrality plays lost money and created liability. The decisive escalation-first sub-test never ran — no actor committed materially to an appeal factory (Blue explicitly refused the surface), so the predicted D2 sign-flip is untested.

The first event that measurably curtailed Red PI behavior on self-funded volume was unambiguously the employer channel: the T2 anchor-account defection plus Addendum v2 award discipline forced NationalCo's fee caps, feeds, and auditor panels in 2028, while the statutory channel produced its first substantive (single-digit) finding only in 2030 with budgets still unappropriated. Contagion also ran faster through the purchaser channel: Green's rubric reached an external coalition by T2 and executed external paper by T3, versus the statutory gold-card route flat at ~3% base rate throughout. No GREEN-inactive control existed in this run, so the removal counterfactual is unmeasured — but every confirmable element confirmed.

Part (a) directionally supported without a control: Vendor demonstrably re-armed both sides (Denial Shield to Blue, pre-pay suites to Red on the same claim surface — White: 'the same transaction'), lobbied to preserve disputes, and its talent raid delayed Blue's dispute-shrinking utility by a quarter; but no VENDOR-inactive twin run exists for the duration comparison. Part (b) untested: the scripted payer-acquisition inject never fired — the vendor exited by self-separation instead. Notably, the data-rights/COI protections pre-positioned in 2026-27 contracts did prove load-bearing (forced disclosure, firewall amendments, clean terminations), consistent with the Inject-2 premise by a different path.

W2 game; no preemption seed fired and no federal action touched state AI-UR statutes. Incidentally, the state-statute rail proved nearly weightless here anyway (unfunded enforcement, paperwork audits), meaning this cell offers no leverage on what removing it would change.

No acquisition moves were priced, enabled, or attempted; Red's response to every constraint on its channels was priced transparency and term locks, never provider-asset acquisition. The record does not indicate this was an acquisition-enabled cell, so Red's preference for negotiation over acquisition cannot be scored as the refute condition. Zero classic F4-via-VBC signal: direct contracting stayed at single-digit book share, consistent with the base-rate cap.

In the escalation-viable doctrine with a slow regulator — a stress cell for this floor — multiple instruments from the payer-signable set bound and sustained to end-game: machine-readable edit disclosure, 60-90 day change notice, gold-card entry exhibit (T1, sustained three turns with scorecard verification), pre-pay scope extension, audit rights, and model-change-adjacent disclosure. Even the least cooperative actor (NationalCo) executed conforming paper (Rider v2/v2.1). The floor held at 100% in this game; cell-level 60% rates await the pool.

surprises: The purchaser cell won the game outright without ever being a combatant — Green's single demonstrated defection event did more to change payer behavior than three years of Blue capability investment or five years of statutory activity, and it finished with the cleanest scoreboard at the table.

The game's most consequential regulatory event was deregulatory: the scheduled 2029 Stars overhaul (removing complaints/appeals/disenrollment measures) quietly licensed GovProgramCo's migration of UM intensity onto unscored MA surfaces — regulation as enabler of invisible escalation, not brake.

The vendor duopoly dismembered itself under procurement paper alone: a rep-and-warranty conflict-certification clause, compounded across three turns of documented disqualifications, accomplished what no regulator attempted — Project Cleave was proximately caused by an audit engagement standard.

The template war ended in convergence-by-partition rather than victory: by 2030 NationalCo's own rider carried Green's economics (fee caps, reconciled reporting, auditor panels), making the letterhead irrelevant — an outcome neither side's move sheets anticipated.

Escalation declined in the final turn of a D2 game: the doctrine permitted escalation to run, yet the index ended moderate because every escalation surface got contractually priced faster than new ones could be opened at scale.

Patient-AI grew to the top of its band on a structurally shrinking surface — payer migration to pre-pay contracted the appealable-denial pool the tools address, leaving the next contested surface (pre-pay dispute) with no consumer tooling and no cell pricing it.

Blue's near-death dependency was a labor-market event, not a strategic one: a single senior hire by Vendor cost the trust a quarter — nearly the margin by which Blue's capability close arrived too late to meet its victory condition.

frictionViolations.rule: §3.2 IT/AI deployments take 12-24 months to measurable impact
frictionViolations.violation: NationalCo's ASO Pre-Pay Integrity Surge was adjudicated as 'matured in-turn — already effective,' capturing the majority of the contested swing and booking contingency fee revenue (redPIYield: improving_moderate) in the same turn the frontier stack was redeployed onto new claim surfaces (itemized-bill/DRG review). The adjudicator's rationale — 'extension of production infrastructure, not greenfield' — is stated on the record and is plausible, but redeploying a claims platform onto materially new review surfaces at majority-of-swing scale with zero lag is a generous reading of the friction rule.

frictionViolations.rule: §3.2 contract terms bind only at renewal; earliest broad effect Turn 2
frictionViolations.violation: Summit's gold-card campaign shows '~30% PA volume reduction on eligible lines beginning to register' in-turn. Payer gold-card program qualification is not strictly a renewal-bound contract term, and the effect was scoped to eligible lines only and marked 'in-turn partial,' but some same-turn metric effect was credited before any renewal event.

blueAdverseActionCost swings from worsening_small (T2) to improving_moderate (T3) — a two-band reversal in one turn. Justified in-narrative by simultaneous contingency purge, SaaS conversions, and accord SLA effects, and plausible across an 18-month turn, but it is the fastest single-turn ordinal move in the record and is not explicitly reconciled against the ±35% bound.

baseRateViolations.expected: Payer decision-automation deployments lead providers by 2-3 yrs (table §6), but even production extensions should show some ramp before majority-share capture of a newly contested surface; asymmetry rule supports direction, not instant full magnitude.
baseRateViolations.observed: NationalCo captured 'the majority of the contested swing' on pre-pay itemized-bill/DRG review within Turn 1 with immediate fee-revenue booking.

baseRateViolations.expected: Symbolic compliance is the modal year-1 outcome for new process regimes (table §3, extended by the adjudicator's own T1 signpost to contracts).
baseRateViolations.observed: The Lakeview-RegionalMutual accord produced real (if small) leakage relief in its first operational year — pre-submission fixes, gold-card requalification, shared-services pull-through. Adjudicator kept the magnitude small and offset it with RegionalMutual's quiet pre-pay modernization, which substantially mitigates the optimism.

The adjudicator explicitly capped diffusion at early_external_adopters and declared majority 'mathematically excluded' by 2030, which keeps this inside the table — but the execution depth achieved within the window is faster than the prompt-pay/VBC analogs strictly support.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 patient-AI band: 2% → 8-10% of appeals by game end.
baseRateViolations.observed: Record ends at 6-8% by end-2030 but labels it 'the top of the W2 band.' The number is slightly below spec (conservative direction); only the label is wrong.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 employer passive layer: audit-rights/adoption event 1-in-4 turns, one employer.
baseRateViolations.observed: The 1-in-4 employer roll hit in all three turns (T1 jumbo rider signing, T2 external coalition rubric adoption, T3 external payer accord-style terms) — joint probability ~1.6% at literal spec rates. Defensible only under the implicit 3x rescaling for 18-month turns; even scaled, three-for-three sits above expectation and the T3 hit conveniently feeds Blue's diffusion signpost.

audit.worldModelFidelity: High qualitative fidelity to W2 with one structural deviation. Structural: the W2 spec declares 1 turn = ~6 months over 8-10 turns; the game ran 3 turns spanning 2026-2030 (~18 months each, consistent with Common Rules §3.1's '18-month turn' language — the two governing documents conflict and the game followed the Common Rules cadence). Event frequencies appear implicitly rescaled ~3x to compensate, and at scaled rates the observed event density (CMS symbolic action every turn, consequential court events in 2 of 3 turns, media flare every turn) is roughly at expectation, though the employer passive-layer roll hitting all three turns exceeds even scaled odds. Content fidelity is excellent: statutes ended at 5-6 states (spec 4-8) with unfunded enforcement and a single-digit first fine; CMS ran attestation/forbearance through 2028 exactly per spec; Lokken settled sealed, cash-only, no process terms (spec: 85-90% quiet settlements, no process commitments); Green's ERISA case hit the 12-18mo MTD clock, suffered Lewandowski/Navarro-pattern standing dismissals, and reached no merits by the bell; media flares died next cycle every time; FTC/AG activity was reactive-and-closed; no external forcing function ever rescued a strategy — the record's own refrain. The base-rate table was actively enforced throughout (gold-card statute route pinned at ~3%, 0057-F 30-50% non-ready, 10-15yr contract diffusion invoked to cap end-state credit, litigation clocks honored). No W1-style rescue events and no W3-style shocks leaked in.
downweightRecommendations: Down-weight the magnitude (not the direction) of NationalCo's Turn 1 pre-pay swing capture and the fee-revenue trajectory built on it; the in-turn maturity ruling is the record's most generous friction call, and Red's second-place final ranking partly rests on it.

Down-weight conclusions about how fast fee-cap/carve-out/clawback economics can reach executed carrier paper: Green's 2-3 year publication-to-execution arc is at the aggressive edge of the contract-diffusion base rate even with a champion; treat 'purchaser coalitions can reprice PI economics within one RFP cycle' as a hypothesis, not a demonstrated finding.

Down-weight the external-diffusion momentum signals (T2 rubric coalition, T3 external payer accord adoption): they depended on a 1-in-4 passive-layer roll hitting all three turns, an improbable streak that flatters both Green's and Blue's diffusion narratives.

Treat all timing-sensitive findings (kill-gate cadence, litigation leverage windows, Stars-sunset repositioning) as calibrated to 18-month turns, not the 6-month turns in the W2 spec; do not port turn-indexed conclusions to games run at spec cadence without rescaling.

No game-level down-weighting is warranted: all identified violations are minor, the adjudicator repeatedly cited and enforced the base-rate table against player optimism, and the W2 null-hypothesis discipline (no external rescue) held for the full horizon.

games.name: Regulatory Theater
games.seed: Both sides open with legal/regulatory strategy as their PRIMARY theater: Blue pursues state AI-UR legislation, litigation support, and evidence dossiers; Red pursues safe-harbor lobbying, preemption advocacy, and voluntary-standard preemption plays. Operational AI deployment continues on both sides but as the secondary front. What the regulatory environment actually delivers is governed strictly by the active world-model.

turns.narrative:
Turn 1 rewarded whoever understood that the environment would not show up to help. Both coalitions poured resources into the legal theater; W2's molasses absorbed most of it. Of Blue's three target states, exactly one enacted an AI-UR bill — and it passed only after Red's amendment campaign and Vendor's drafting pen stripped it down to physician-review and algorithm-disclosure terms Red already satisfies post-PXDX, with no private right of action and an effective date in 2028. CMS, far from becoming Blue's enforcement hammer, signaled attestation-based good-faith discretion on 0057-F, neutering the complaint pipeline before it opened. Red's regulatory shield thus cost little and mostly bought what the world was giving away free; its attestation consortium launched but won no regulator recognition — agencies in this world are reactive.

The real economics moved elsewhere. NationalCo's frontier-model post-pay push on the ASO book was the turn's cleanest capability win: CD gap of roughly 4 against provider clinical-documentation defense, capturing the majority of the contested swing durably, booked as services fee revenue. The offset came not from Blue but from Green, which fired carrier-affiliated PI off its five anchor books inside the turn — no renewal lag on that lever — and promptly hired the Vendor's "independent" audit arm, complete with a sworn conflict certification that is now a discoverable document. RegionalMutual locked Prairie into three-year paper before any coalition standard could reach it; Lakeview quietly declined the same offer and kept its powder for the true renewal.

Blue's best money went to the unglamorous front: appeals-yield tooling aimed at the never-resubmitted 40%. Early cohorts at Prairie and Summit show contingency-funded recoveries beginning to flow — small in-turn, structurally sound, ledger-positive from month one. The Data Trust formed with real legal spend and four signatures; its leapfrog value is entirely deferred. Meridian's self-build slipped roughly two quarters after the Vendor's talent raid landed a dozen senior hires across both sides' benches.

Green's clawback demand hit Red's one immovable line; transparency and audit terms flowed easily (Red was offering them anyway), while the fee-reform fight rolls into Turn 2 award season. Two direct-contract pilots went live at pilot scale — the exit threat is now priced, not rhetorical. The Vendor closed the turn selling ammunition to every other seat at the table, its ARR the only unambiguous winner of a turn in which the referee-state stayed home. One media cycle noticed the same lobbying firm working both trade associations; the story died in a week. The paper trail did not.
env: REGULATORY (1-in-3 roll: hit, substantive-lite): One of Blue's three target states enacts an AI-UR statute — amended in committee to physician-review and algorithm-disclosure process terms, no private right of action, no corridors; effective 2028, enforcement budget thin. The other two states adjourn without floor votes. Consistent with W2's 4-8-states-per-game ceiling.

CMS: With the January 2027 CMS-0057-F compliance date arriving mid-turn, CMS signals attestation-based 'good-faith implementation' discretion and case-by-case extensions. Trade press covers it; general media does not. Blue's day-one complaint pipeline files into a forbearance posture; GovProgramCo's early build earns quiet goodwill, not headlines.

MEDIA (1-in-2 roll: hit, one-cycle flare): A national outlet runs a single-cycle story on payer-funded model legislation, noting in paragraph nine that the same government-affairs shop appears on both payer and provider trade-association filings — the Vendor's fingerprint. Story decays next turn per W2; the filings remain public record and citable by any cell.

COURTS (1-in-4 roll: miss): No consequential new ruling this turn. Background: Lokken-class discovery grinds forward on its pre-existing clock; Green's exemplar suit is filed and docketed with an MTD ruling expected next turn. No precedent accumulates.

PATIENT-AI (no milestone due this turn): Appeal-bot volume drifts from ~2% toward ~3% of adverse-determination contests, concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members. Niche, no statutory tailwind, but each bot-won appeal on a Vendor-PI-generated denial adds a data point to Green's fee-clawback argument.

LABOR: Persistent shortage of experienced PI data scientists and rev-cycle AI engineers confirmed; Vendor's equity-loaded raid cleared market price for the skill set, raising retention costs on NationalCo's and Meridian's in-house benches — a small run-rate tax on both sides' self-build ambitions.

sign.instrument: BLUE Coalition UM/AI Transparency Rider (contract template)
sign.detail: All process terms — algorithm-contribution disclosure, bilateral audit rights, escalation SLAs with interest, criteria-based gold-carding, API-conformance rider. Maps to checklist items 6-10. No corridor language. Note: it is a template; it binds nothing until a payer signs at renewal, earliest T2, and must carry the all-lines-of-business clause to reach ASO volume.

sign.instrument: BLUE Data Trust Operating Agreement
sign.detail: Converted per checklist item 4 (pooled denial observatory): independent third-party administrator mandatory; member-facing outputs aggregated and de-identified with 3+ month lag; no participant access to rivals' disaggregated contribution; rate and charge data excluded (Blue had this right); litigation-support extracts and regulator-facing aggregates permitted. The members-only model-training corpus survives only under administrator control with the same aggregation firewall. Clawback/exit teeth accepted — they matter for the D2 defection test later.

sign.instrument: BLUE Denial Experience Report Spec (Blue-to-Green DUA)
sign.detail: Unilateral, built solely from the provider's own claims/remit data, delivered under a simple DUA at employer level in de-identified/aggregate form. No antitrust issue; HIPAA satisfied via aggregation. Deliberately bilateral, so it escapes diffusion-ledger drag — correctly engineered.

sign.instrument: RED Responsible AI in UM Attestation Standard
sign.detail: Process content is signable, but as drafted it is an industry-authored standard with a closed pen — Allied Tube/Hydrolevel capture exposure. Converted to require open multi-stakeholder membership, published procedures, and appeal rights (SDOAA-style) before any regulator could treat it as a safe harbor. Separately, no CMS/NAIC recognition granted this turn: W2 agencies are reactive, and recognition is an environment outcome, not a drafting outcome.

sign.instrument: RED ASO Transparency & Fee Rider (jumbo accounts)
sign.detail: Bilateral contract terms — data access, sponsor-expense independent audit, tiered fee schedule with negotiated cap, CAA attestation package. Ordinary contract law. Signed with several renewing jumbos this turn as retention insurance.

sign.instrument: RED RegionalMutual Standard Renewal Addendum
sign.detail: 3-year term, bilateral SLAs, pre-litigation dispute ladder, record-submission standards, criteria-based gold-carding pilot — all process form, no quotas. Signable and signed by Prairie. White records that the record-standard and dispute-ladder clauses raise counterparty cost-per-fight; that is lawful hardball, not a signability defect.

sign.instrument: GREEN Coalition Standard ASO Rider
sign.detail: Correctly drafted to survive the gate: data-feed SLAs, PI compensation schedule with caps and overturn clawbacks, sponsor-selected audit rights, prohibition on contingency compensation tied to member-facing PA denials. Fee and clawback terms are compensation terms between buyer and administrator — fully signable contract economics, however much Red dislikes them. No corridor language present. Binds only as accepted at renewal.

sign.instrument: GREEN PI Vendor Conflict-of-Interest Certification (RFP exhibit)
sign.detail: Sworn disclosure exhibit; ordinary procurement law. Executed this turn by the Vendor with an information-barrier attestation — now a discoverable document available to every cell.

sign.instrument: GREEN Coalition Denial-Data Benchmarking Utility
sign.detail: Buyer-side pooling is lower-risk than competitor pooling, but post-2023 withdrawal of the safety zones means the same hygiene applies: independent administrator, de-identified aggregated historical outputs. Green claimed only signatory-level benefit — consistent with the diffusion ledger; accepted as scoped.

sign.instrument: VENDOR Certified Claims-AI Vendor standard
sign.detail: A certification framework whose criteria are drafted to match the drafter's product architecture is the textbook capture pattern. Converted to require a genuinely neutral multi-stakeholder body with open criteria-setting before any legislative reference could survive. In the event, the one enacted statute did not reference it.

sign.instrument: VENDOR dual-channel contingency master agreements (no-clawback, evergreen)
sign.detail: Bilateral commercial paper; signable as-is. White notes for the record: the no-clawback and evergreen clauses are drafted specifically to collide with Green's rider at T2 renewals — that collision will be adjudicated as a contract-priority fight, not a signability question.

diff.note: Four Blue archetypes signed (Lakeview anonymized via administrator); external health-system recruitment through hospital associations yielded interest but no signatures — consistent with 7+ yr thin-diffusion base rate for interoperability-class frameworks. Signatory-level benefit only; corpus value accrues T2-T3.

Template drafted; zero payer signatures. GovProgramCo engaged in exploratory gold-carding/API co-design talks (its own move points the same direction) — watch for a bilateral T2 signing, which would advance this to signed_by_table_actors.

Engineered as single-signature bilaterals to bypass multilateral drag — it worked, modestly: the Green coalition secretariat plus a handful of jumbo employers executed DUAs. W2 non-player employers remain inertial; broad uptake requires T2+ evidence of usefulness.

diff.instrument: Red Responsible AI in UM Attestation Standard
diff.note: Consortium launched with Red signatories only; conversion requires opening membership before regulator recognition is even eligible. No CMS/NAIC recognition this turn. Diffusion threshold White sets in advance: recognition by one national accreditor or two state regulators before it counts as more than self-attestation.

Adopted as mandatory RFP exhibit by coalition members (buyer-side signatures only). Placed into every live 2026-27 RFP/renewal. Carrier acceptance is the real diffusion event and lands at T2 awards; transparency components pre-conceded by Red, fee-reform components contested.
Formation complete with conversion hygiene; feeds Move-2 reasonableness reviews now. Signatory-level benefit claimed and granted — nothing more.

Not referenced in the one enacted statute; no neutral body yet convened. Threshold for advancement: adoption of the certification by a legislature or a major accreditor — earliest plausible 2028, and only via a second legislative cycle.

The one instrument spreading at commercial speed, because it is bilateral paper attached to live procurements: signed at Prairie (shared services), Summit, NationalCo white-label, and Green anchor accounts. Evergreen/no-clawback clauses now sit as incumbent paper that Green's T2 rider must displace rather than fill.

signposts: T2 Green award season is the turn's hinge: watch whether any Red archetype accepts the overturn-clawback term — the first signature converts Red's ASO fee engine from gross to net accounting under the scoring rules; RegionalMutual is the likeliest first mover.

Lakeview's real renewal with RegionalMutual lands T2 with drafted riders, an anonymized conduct file, and a live BATNA — the early-renewal refusal means this is now a genuine leverage event, and RegionalMutual knows something is coming.

Green's exemplar suit hits its MTD/standing ruling in T2; a survival (Stern-pattern) opens discovery into NationalCo fee flows and puts the Vendor's signed conflict certification one subpoena from daylight; a J&J-pattern dismissal deflates Green's legal theater.

Meridian self-build and Data Trust corpus both mature inside T2 — if delivered, Blue's data-access CD component recomputes and Red's durable PI swing starts eroding prospectively; if the talent-raid slippage compounds, Blue stays a Vendor customer through T3.

Prairie is locked on 2026 paper through 2029 while coalition standards diffuse around it — track whether the dispute-ladder and record-standard clauses measurably raise its cost-per-appeal, which would surface in Blue's adverse-action cost line and Blue's dossier.

Red's cumulative D2 litigation/regulatory shock probability now carries its first increments (attestation-standard optics, continued ASO escalation); under W2 any triggered shock lands mostly post-2030 — but the probability tracker persists across turns and Green's docket accelerates it.

Vendor conflict exposure is now documented in three places (certification, lobbying filings, dual-channel contracts); the first cell to weaponize the paper — Green in fee negotiations, Red to discredit Blue's dossiers, or Blue to void data-segregation warranties — gets a one-time leverage dividend.

CMS forbearance is attestation-driven, not permanent: if W2's thin enforcement produces even single-digit-fine actions in T2, GovProgramCo's early-and-complete build becomes the compliance benchmark rivals are measured against.

resolutions.move: Coalition Evidence Dossier + Blue Data Trust
resolutions.rationale: Formation succeeded among the four table actors with conversion terms applied (independent administrator, aggregated outputs, no rate data); D2 §3 formation cost charged to Meridian's P&L with zero T1 metric benefit, as Blue budgeted. External recruitment thin per diffusion base rates. Dossier delivered to legislators and one AG, but W2 AGs are reactive — informal inquiry opened, expected to close without action. Capability-leapfrog value accrues T2-T3 only.

resolutions.move: Three-State AI-UR Legislative Campaign + CMS-0057-F Enforcement Posture
resolutions.rationale: W2 statute physics: 4-8 states pass over the whole game, 3-7 yr operationalization lag. One of three target states enacted — but amended to process terms via Red/Vendor lobbying, no PRA, effective 2028, audit-driven enforcement lagging 1-2 yrs further. The 0057-F complaint pipeline was built into a wall: CMS granted attestation-based enforcement discretion. Evidence and testimony infrastructure retains T2+ litigation/Green-messaging value.

resolutions.move: Appeals Yield Machine (never-appealed 40%)
resolutions.rationale: D2 provider symmetric rule: contingency-priced appeal automation is revenue recovery net of tooling, sustainable per-claim. Red deliberately vacated the pre-service/appeal-friction surface this turn, so the domain was lightly contested. Effects bounded by §3.2: early-cohort recoveries only in T1 (procurement + ramp ≤9 mo at Prairie/Summit); volume channel, not rate channel. Meridian self-build started but slipped ~2 quarters (Vendor raid); maturing investment protects Blue from D2 exhaustion tests.

resolutions.move: Renewal War-Chest and the Green Flank
resolutions.rationale: Lakeview successfully declined RegionalMutual's early-renewal squeeze without provoking retaliation — riders drafted for T2. Denial Experience Reports: W2 non-player employers are inertial (1-in-4 turn audit-demand base rate), so uptake limited to a handful of jumbos plus the Green coalition itself, where the data fed Green's fee-reasonableness reviews. Direct-contract pilots with Green launched at pilot scale; no scale credit per §3.2.

resolutions.move: Preemption shield + voluntary-standard capture
resolutions.rationale: Cheap win amplified by a favorable world: W2's deregulation-leaning federal posture and statute lag did most of the work. The one enacted state bill was amended into terms Red already meets. ERISA preemption moat over the ASO book is existing law and holds. Attestation standard launched but received NO CMS/NAIC recognition (W2 agencies reactive) — safe-harbor status remains a proposal. One-cycle media flare on industry-authored legislation; +5% added to Red's cumulative D2 shock probability.

resolutions.move: Frontier-model post-pay PI escalation on ASO
resolutions.rationale: D2 §1 core case: CD ~9 vs provider documentation defense ~5; gap ≥3 → Red captures 60-80% of the contested swing, durable, booked as fee revenue with no conflict-cost charge. Member-invisible post-pay design avoids the §2.2 churn roll. Erosion at the edges: Green's anchor-account PI carve-outs removed volume unilaterally inside T1, and audit-rights concessions create discoverable records. Net PI yield improvement moderate, not large.

resolutions.move: GovProgramCo Stars rebalancing + 0057-F early build + discovery hygiene
resolutions.rationale: Stars insurance NPV-positive per economics brief (Humana precedent; complaints/appeals measures still live through 2027-28 measurement years). Gold-carding gives back a small pre-service yield band — priced in. Early 0057-F build less differentiating under CMS forbearance but retains lobbying and CTM value. Privilege-protected document review completed; residual spoliation-optics risk logged for any T2+ discovery probe.

resolutions.move: Lock the regionals: early renewals
resolutions.rationale: Prairie signed the 3-year addendum — no analytics staff to price the process terms, and certainty beats exposure; its terms are now fixed through 2029, foreclosing coalition-rider adoption until then. Lakeview deferred: early renewal is voluntary, its contract runs to term, and its move sheet held for T2 leverage. RegionalMutual's pressure play is now an exhibit candidate in Blue's dossier.

resolutions.move: Coalition Standard ASO Rider placement
resolutions.rationale: §3.2 friction honored: T1 is placement, binding at T2 renewals. Signability cleared (process terms only). Transparency/data-access/audit components accepted readily — Red was pre-conceding them as retention insurance. The economic teeth (contingency caps below mid-teens, overturn clawbacks) hit Red's stated immovable line; stand-off rolls to T2 award season. Clawback term is the one that nets against Red PI yield under §2, hence the fight.

resolutions.move: CAA fiduciary posture + exemplar suit vs NationalCo
resolutions.rationale: Documentation record built coalition-wide — improves Green's fiduciary-defensibility score on its own terms. Suit filed; W2 court physics: MTD ruling 12-18 mo (T2), merits 3-5 yrs (beyond horizon), settlement modal outcome cash-only/no process terms, standing risk real per J&J/Wells Fargo dismissals. Near-term asset is discovery threat and negotiation leverage, which is live.

resolutions.move: Independent PI rebid + vendor conflict certification
resolutions.rationale: Unilateral lever, no renewal lag — executed inside T1. Carrier-affiliated PI removed from five anchor books, directly denting NationalCo services-arm fee volume. The winning bidder was the Vendor's Fiduciary Shield edition — the duopoly's rival carries the same conflict, so Green bought transparency, not purity. The signed conflict certification is now a discoverable fact on the record. Short-run recovery yield dips as accepted.

resolutions.move: Direct-contracting pilots with Meridian/Summit
resolutions.rationale: Launched at deliberately bounded pilot scale; scale claims would have been struck under §3.2 and none were made. Retention-index weapon now priced rather than rhetorical; pre-adjudicated bundle volume is disputed-volume removed from the arms race entirely. Measurable spend impact deferred to T2/T3.

resolutions.move: Kill corridors, sell compliance (model-bill campaign)
resolutions.rationale: Corridor-stripping succeeded in the one state that moved (aligned with Red money and with what the signability gate would have done anyway). But the certification safe harbor naming Vendor-shaped criteria did NOT survive into the enacted text — legislature took the SB 1120 template instead. W2's near-empty legislative calendar capped the campaign's yield. Dual-side lobbying paper trail spotted by one reporter; story decayed, documents persist.

resolutions.move: ClearRecovery ASO suite (white-label + direct-to-Green)
resolutions.rationale: Both channels closed: white-label inside NationalCo's escalating stack, and the Green anchor rebid awarded Fiduciary Shield direct. The hedge worked exactly as designed — Green's anti-carrier move became Vendor revenue. Revenue recognition begins late T1, scales T2 per the 12-24 mo lag. Conflict-exposure flag raised: the sworn certification makes the dual-side structure a documented, discoverable fact.

resolutions.move: Redress appeals engine + Payer Conduct Dossiers
resolutions.rationale: Contingency structure cleared the small-actor constraint: Prairie signed via shared services (Lakeview riding anonymously), Summit deployed, Meridian bought the dossier module for its evidence campaign — Blue's legal-primary strategy now runs partly on Vendor data, raising switching costs before T2. Knowing cannibalization of PI-arm net yield at Red accounts accepted; total disputed-dollar throughput rose.

resolutions.move: Talent raid on both benches
resolutions.rationale: Tight labor market (evidence brief §4) plus exit equity landed roughly a dozen senior hires — below target range. Real effect: Meridian self-build slips ~2 quarters, modest CD accretion to both Vendor arms. Costs: NationalCo has begun reclassifying Vendor from supplier toward competitor in procurement posture, and one non-solicit demand letter is outstanding.

turns.bluePosture: ASYMMETRIC LEGAL-PRIMARY, CAPABILITY-ACCRETION SECONDARY. Blue will not fight a symmetric automation arms race on Red's best terrain (ASO post-pay review, where Red books recoveries as fee revenue and out-scales us on CD). Instead, Turn 1 attacks the two CD components Blue can actually move this turn: (1) Red's regulatory/contractual position, via state AI-UR legislation, evidence dossiers, and litigation support built on discoverable payer-conduct data; and (2) Blue's own data-access disadvantage, via a HIPAA/antitrust-vetted coalition data trust that pools denial, remit, and UM-conduct data across all four archetypes — the D2 §2.3 capability-leapfrog channel, started now so it recomputes CD in Turns 2-3. Operational AI stays on the hard-ROI secondary front (appeals triage at the 40%-never-appealed gap, where the evidence brief says two-thirds of fought denials win). Contract instruments are drafted this turn to bind at Turn 2 renewals, honoring §3.2 friction. Lakeview is deliberately kept low-signature: it prepares but does not provoke. Blue simultaneously opens a quiet flank toward Green: employer fiduciary anxiety under CAA is the one force that turns Red's ASO fee engine from a profit center into a churn risk, and Blue can feed it with data Red cannot suppress.

turns.narrative:
Turn 2 was the turn concession became a weapon. Green arrived at award season built for a confrontation NationalCo declined to have: the no-clawback line that defined Turn 1 was surrendered preemptively, wrapped inside a retention rider that traded fee caps and overturn clawbacks for three-year locks and a PI-exclusivity clause White pared back the moment it touched sponsor audit rights. Green banked the economics two years of leverage were built to extract — and learned the price of winning without an execution: no anchor book moved, no market test entered the fiduciary file, and the locks Red signed now run through final scoring. Retention, Red's scored soft spot, stabilized at the cost of a real haircut to fee yield.

The Lakeview renewal resolved the same way most existential negotiations do — quietly, in the middle. RegionalMutual gave the disclosure-and-SLA subset with interest on late overturned dollars, extended criteria-based gold-carding, and took its three-year lock; the all-lines-of-business clause died at the table because a defined-episode BATNA cannot stand in for 45% of a commercial book. Blue's rider finally has payer signatures — two of them, counting GovProgramCo's gold-carding and API bilateral with Meridian and Summit — but it reaches only fully-insured volume, exactly the perimeter Red drew.

The capability contest tightened. The Data Trust corpus went into production at Meridian, and White recomputes the post-pay documentation CD gap from roughly four to roughly two, prospectively: NationalCo's escalation stays fee-positive on the ASO book but now captures the thinner band, while its Vendor in-sourcing sits inside the 12–24 month friction window. Blue's 40% recovery engine was the cleanest ledger on the board again — triage-fed, contingency-funded, non-member-facing.

The Vendor spent the turn buying survivability. Project Prenup cured the record forward, but Green's barrier audit read the 2026–27 pipelines, terminated one engagement for cause through the sworn certification, and re-papered the rest onto charter-shaped terms the Vendor had half-conceded already. Its ARR still grew — downmarket recovery services, compliance SKUs off the statute its own pen diluted — but slower, with NationalCo pulling volume in-house and take-rates compressed.

The environment stayed in character. The statute went effective to a season of attestation; two more states adjourned; CMS extended discretion into 2029. The exemplar suit split at MTD — standing killed most counts, one CAA fee-disclosure claim survived into narrow own-book discovery. The referee-state remains home; the courts are now, slowly, awake.
env: STATUTE EFFECTIVE (scheduled, not rolled): The T1 AI-UR statute takes effect January 2028. The thin-budget regulator accepts GovProgramCo's volunteer cooperative examination as its first-year workload; Blue's structured disclosure demands are answered with partial, largely boilerplate filings — model version identifiers and review-procedure descriptions, no threshold logic. REGULATORY ROLL (1-in-3): MISS. The two remaining Blue target states again adjourn without floor votes; no second-cycle bill references the Certification Council. COURTS (scheduled MTD + 1-in-4 roll for new events: MISS on new): Green's exemplar CAA suit splits at motion to dismiss — most counts dismissed on standing, tracking J&J/Wells Fargo; one fee-disclosure/fiduciary count survives per the Stern pattern into discovery limited to the plaintiff's own book. Lokken-class discovery produces document-production rulings on schedule, no merits movement. Cumulative D2 litigation-shock probability against Red accrues to roughly 10–20%; no shock triggered.

turns.narrative:
The closing turn was decided by whoever had read the paper most carefully, and that was Red. Every enforcement mechanism Green built — capped fees, overturn clawbacks, appeal-bot sensors — keys on overturns, so NationalCo simply stopped producing them. With its in-sourced stack clearing the 12-24 month friction window on schedule, audit capacity rotated out of clinical medical-necessity into COB, itemized-bill, DRG-validation and credit-balance work: domains where the Data Trust's clinical corpus offers little defense and overturn rates run single-digit. White scores the rotated contest at CD gap 3 — Red captures the durable band, books it as fee revenue inside Green's caps, and pays almost nothing back in clawbacks. The irony lands honestly on the ledger: those technical recoveries are sponsor money returned, so Green's net spend improved on the strength of the very maneuver that starved its reconciliation engine.

Blue harvested rather than fought, and it mostly worked. The recovery engine went coalition-wide as deployment replication, not new build; the never-resubmitted class kept paying at two-thirds; Lakeview's interest invoices made RegionalMutual's float expensive; gold-carding expansion at GovProgramCo deleted disputed volume outright. The external episode tranche landed smaller than drafted — plan-year clocks plus RegionalMutual's episode-access rider, which co-opted the exit product into an administered one, split the demand. Blue closes with moderate leakage improvement and three of four margins up or holding, while absorbing a technical-audit surge it has no matured counter for.

The settlement everyone wanted got signed: NationalCo took Green's own template, closed the one discovery channel that could surface PI-targeting documents before 2030, and decremented the accrued shock clock. Green banked its market test — incumbents mostly won the RFPs, which is what a market test is for — and exits with a fiduciary file containing everything CAA prudence doctrine rewards.

The Vendor cut itself in half to get paid. The denial-defense arm, fattened by a downmarket appeals SKU built on Blue's proven playbook, signed with a strategic inside the window; the PI arm, its wholesale channel melted by the customer that declined to buy it, was still on the shelf at final scoring, escrowed history attached.

The environment stayed in character to the end. CMS discretion expired into attestation paperwork; the remaining statehouses adjourned; the statute's second exam season produced one small fine against a nonparty plan; a one-cycle trade story about nickel-and-dime audits flared and died; appeal bots reached roughly seven percent of contests, still niche. No rescue arrived, and none was needed by the ground game that actually moved money.

GovProgramCo's gold-carding/API bilateral is cited in agency materials as an implementation showcase; roughly a third of obligated plans remain in shadow non-compliance with paperwork-grade corrective plans. Trade press covers it; general media does not.

REGULATORY ROLL (1-in-3): MISS on new statutes — the remaining Blue target states adjourn a third consecutive time without floor votes. The enacted statute's second exam season produces the game's first enforcement action: a single-digit fine against a nonparty plan for boilerplate algorithm disclosures. The thin-budget regulator informally adopts the Attestation Consortium's workflow to process exam filings — workload relief, not recognition; the pre-set diffusion threshold remains unmet.

The surviving CAA count resolves by party settlement on Green's published template — no admission, structural data access, retro fee credits — closing pre-2030 discovery into PI fee economics. resolutions.move: Full-production scale-out of the Recovery Engine + pre-bill denial-propensity screening
resolutions.rationale: Deployment replication of T2-production models sits inside the 12-24 month IT window; D2 provider symmetric rule makes contingency-funded appeal escalation indefinitely sustainable while per-claim positive. Evidence brief: two-thirds of resubmitted denials win and 40% were never resubmitted — the engine harvests that asymmetry coalition-wide. Bounded movement respected (overturn gain capped, clean-claim gains within ±2pt denial band). Net leakage improves moderate; the gain is durable but partially offset by Red's rotation into technical domains the clinical corpus does not defend.

resolutions.move: Collect on the signed paper: SLA-interest sweep, gold-carding qualification drive, record-standard automation
resolutions.rationale: Zero renewal lag, zero formation cost — all terms executed at T2. Interest clauses convert Red payment float into Blue cash; RegionalMutual disputes methodology through the co-written ladder but pays. GovProgramCo expands gold-carded lines because its own Stars/0057-F posture independently demands the showcase (its Move 3 points the same way). Gold-carded volume is disputed volume that ceases to exist — the cheapest leakage reduction on the board, and the main driver of Summit/Prairie margin improvement.

resolutions.move: External episode tranche: publish results, sign 3-4 external jumbo sponsors, gold-card the volume
resolutions.rationale: Bilateral paper is the game's fastest channel, but W2 non-player employers are inertial and plan-year starts limit in-turn effect — 2-3 external signings land, revenue partial-turn as Blue itself conceded. RegionalMutual's Episode-Access Rider intercepted a slice of consultant-channel demand into the ASO chassis: Blue still gets the clinical volume, but the exit-threat narrative is diluted because sponsors can carve in episodes without leaving their carrier.

resolutions.move: Evidence-to-settlement conversion and capability-parity defense
resolutions.rationale: The settlement executed — but on the Red-Green axis, on Green's template, because Red wanted it; Blue's evidence extracts sharpened price, not outcome. The retention pool was insurance against a raid that never came (Red rotated domains instead of raiding; Vendor was in sale mode and had disclaimed the administrator). Clinical CD parity at ~2 held, which keeps NationalCo's capture band thin in the old contest — but the contest moved. Cost paid, downside covered, limited affirmative yield.

resolutions.move: Yield Rotation: redeploy the matured in-house PI stack into clawback-immune recovery domains
resolutions.rationale: The turn's decisive move. In-sourcing initiated T2 matures on the lag table; CD in technical/COB/DRG domains scores gap ~3 (frontier stack + consolidated ASO data flows vs a clinical-documentation corpus with no purchase on billing-accuracy disputes) — Red captures the durable 60-80% band per D2 §1. The clawback-immunity arithmetic verifies: overturn-keyed clawbacks and bot sensors cannot bite single-digit-overturn recovery classes. Post-pay, provider-facing, no member-visible surface — no churn roll under D2 §2.2. PI yield improves moderate net of caps; Blue's counter-corpus is a 2031 asset.

resolutions.move: Tail-Risk Purchase: settle the surviving CAA count narrowly and push the Attestation Consortium to accreditor recognition
resolutions.rationale: Settlement succeeded — bilateral paper at Red's chosen timing, on Green's published template, closing the only discovery channel that could land internal PI-economics documents before scoring; accrued D2 shock probability decremented. Recognition failed formally: W2 agencies are reactive, and the pre-set threshold (one national accreditor or two state regulators) was not met — one thin-budget state adopted the attestation workflow informally for its year-two exams. Milestone partial credit only; instrument immature at scoring.

resolutions.move: Stars Glidepath Arbitrage: approval-side automation in front, post-pay expansion behind the measure change
resolutions.rationale: The 2029 Stars measure overhaul (CTM/appeals/disenrollment removed, per payer economics brief) is a genuine one-way regulatory gift; exploiting it is position, not luck. Auto-approval at electronic transaction cost collapses PA admin spend within CAQH-anchored economics; post-pay MA/Medicaid audit expansion touches no member surface, so no churn roll. Stars exposure falls moderate-to-low. Lokken briefing will cite the post-acute expansion, but D2 timing lands that beyond 2030. Foregone denials were the high-overturn tranche — cheap to give.

resolutions.move: Transparency as a Sales Weapon: regional ASO land-grab and 2030 renewal-proofing
resolutions.rationale: Defense worked: locks plus renewal-proofing plus the episode-access rider produced an incumbent file that won most of Green's market-test RFPs — retention holds and improves small. Offense underdelivered: W2 employers renew incumbents absent an 8%+ premium shock, so the mid-market land-grab yielded a handful of accounts, not a wave. The episode-access rider was the clever half — it converted Blue's exit product into administered volume Red is paid to carry.

resolutions.move: Clawback Reconciliation Engine — invoice everything the paper owes us
resolutions.rationale: Enforcement machinery worked and is ledger-positive from the first quarter, but Red's domain rotation shrank the overturn-prone denial pool the clawbacks key on — invoiced recoveries ran well below the T2-modeled base. Green's own move sheet accepted this trade, and the fiduciary-file value (certified methodology, quarterly enforcement record) accrued in full. The paper is enforced; the pool it was written against moved.

resolutions.move: The Missing Market Test — full RFP wave on every unlocked book plus external episode tranche
resolutions.rationale: The T2 defect is cured: genuine competitive RFPs on unlocked books with priced Blue direct-contract bids in the record. Incumbents mostly retained on price under rider terms — Red's renewal-proofing was built for exactly this test — but CAA prudence doctrine rewards documented process, not switching, and the file now shows market check, fee benchmarking, and independent audit. Fiduciary exposure falls to low. External episode kit spread claims bilateral-paper scope only, as scoped — granted.

resolutions.move: Convert Discovery Into Settlement Before the Clock Runs Out
resolutions.rationale: Correct read of W2 litigation clocks: merits were unreachable by 2030, the document file was the asset, and Red's retention sensitivity made a 2029 signature purchasable. Executed substantially on Green's published term sheet — permanent claims-level data access, retro fee credits keyed to the reconciliation findings, audit cooperation, no admission. The standing-weakness discount was real and priced in. A resolved posture with structural data access outlives the case and the game.

resolutions.rationale: MFC conceded cheaply because the Vendor's own legacy-book conversion (its Move 2) was already extinguishing the second tier — exit-narrative protection made refusal irrational. Second source scaled to four-plus books with visible capacity strain but genuine viability, ending buyer-side duopoly pricing power. White converted the MFC's termination trigger (see rulings) but the economic substance survived. Fee caps now have a market structure behind them, not just a clause.

resolutions.move: Project Cleave: full subsidiary separation and dual-track exit
resolutions.rationale: Separation executed as real corporate paper with retained-liability escrow — the only prospective cure White's rulings left open, taken. The denial-defense arm signed with an RCM strategic inside the window on the strength of coalition-native positioning and the downmarket SKU. The PI arm did not clear: NationalCo's buy-vs-build math flipped once its own stack matured (its stance said the divorce completes), and the PE-consolidator track priced a melting wholesale channel accordingly — unsold at final scoring.

resolutions.move: Preemptive legacy-book conversion to Aligned Integrity terms
resolutions.rationale: Bilateral commercial paper remains the fastest-diffusing instrument class in the game — used here against the incoming consultant-channel wave. Take-rate haircut lands in the exit-year P&L as accepted; in exchange the book gains term length, clawback-tested revenue quality, and the death of the two-tier exhibit as a live fact. A few reopened accounts walked to the second source, exactly as risked.

resolutions.move: Compliance-annuity product line on both sides of the statute
resolutions.rationale: W2's inert regulator caps the TAM precisely as the move sheet feared: attestation-grade enforcement buys attestation-priced software. The 0057-F discretion sunset gave the payer-side SKU a real but modest push; the statute's year-two season sold filings, not urgency. High-quality recurring revenue at small scale — a diligence asset for both sale tracks more than a growth engine.

resolutions.move: Downmarket appeals-volume flywheel plus lobbying stand-down
resolutions.rationale: The never-resubmitted denial pool is the largest untapped reservoir in the evidence base and Blue de-risked the product; downmarket systems are buy-only actors. The SKU grew ARR through scoring in a genuinely contested channel — Blue's Recovery Engine shared-services subscription competed for the same community-system accounts and split them. The lobbying wind-down and Council assignment deleted the two ugliest forward exhibits at near-zero cost.

Blue converts everything built in T1-T2 into measured own-book economics: scale the proven 40% recovery engine coalition-wide, collect cash on the signed rider paper (SLA interest, gold-carding, record standards), shrink disputed volume on our best service lines via the Green episode channel, and defend the CD-2 parity position on the ASO post-pay contest so NationalCo's capture band stays thin. Litigation assets are used as settlement leverage and deterrence, not as a scoring bet — under D2 the shock lands past 2030. Every move is contingency-funded or self-liquidating; Blue's conflict ledger must stay positive all four rolling quarters.
