rapporteur.excursionSummary:
GAME B1G3 (D2 escalation-viable doctrine, W2 slow-referee world) opened with both coalitions committing their primary theater to law and regulation, and the world declined to show up. Of Blue's three target states, one enacted a statute stripped to terms Red already satisfied; CMS chose attestation-based forbearance three years running; courts moved on their own clocks, killing most of Green's exemplar suit on standing. The seeded legal-primary posture was devalued by the end of Turn 1, and every actor that pivoted fastest to private ordering and unit economics profited.

The real contest ran on two rails. First, a capability race: NationalCo's frontier-model post-pay push on the ASO book opened a CD gap of roughly 4; Blue's pooled Data Trust corpus clawed it back to roughly 2 by 2028; Red then rotated its matured, in-sourced stack into technical recovery domains (COB, DRG validation, itemized-bill, credit-balance) where Blue's clinical corpus offered no defense, re-opening a CD-3 band through scoring. Second, a paper race: Green weaponized award season to force fee caps and overturn clawbacks - and Red defused the confrontation by conceding preemptively, wrapping the concession in three-year locks that ran past final scoring. The decisive endgame insight was Red's: every enforcement mechanism on the board (clawbacks, appeal-bot sensors) keyed on overturns, so Red stopped producing overturns, escalating instead in single-digit-overturn technical domains that were simultaneously clawback-immune and member-invisible.

Numeric corridors never reached any table; process terms bound everywhere - disclosure, SLAs with interest, criteria-based gold-carding, audit rights, capped fees - through three separate commercial channels, including Red voluntarily selling as an ASO sales differentiator the very transparency substance it refused to have compelled on ASO lines. Blue's best money was its least glamorous: the never-resubmitted-40% appeals engine was ledger-positive from month one and scaled coalition-wide. The Vendor, Turn 1's only unambiguous winner, spent Turns 2-3 buying survivability from its own discoverable conflict record, split itself, and sold half.

At scoring, every actor's headline metrics were flat-to-improving while the escalation index stayed elevated - a profitable, professionalized, member-invisible war of attrition governed by bilateral contract rather than by the state, with the decisive battles (2031-32 renewal cycle, technical counter-corpus, gross-recovery clawback triggers, Lokken class certification) all deferred past the horizon.
rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By end-2030 the conflict has neither resolved nor exploded; it has professionalized and gone underground. Adversarial payment-integrity activity continues at elevated intensity, but it has been deliberately rotated onto surfaces that no enforcement mechanism, regulator, scoring metric, or patient tool can see: low-overturn technical recoveries (COB, DRG validation, itemized-bill review, credit balances) on self-funded volume, booked as fee revenue. Member-facing denials and prior authorization are quiet - not from peace but from arbitrage, because those were the only surfaces anyone measured. The regulatory state is functionally absent: one thin statute produced attestation-grade compliance and a single small fine; CMS forbearance rolled forward; courts delivered one narrow settled count. In the state's absence, a dense private-ordering layer emerged and became the operative rulebook: bilateral process-term paper (algorithm disclosure, escalation SLAs with interest, criteria-based gold-carding, audit rights, capped fees, overturn clawbacks) diffusing at commercial speed through renewal riders, vendor repricing, and employer RFP exhibits - while every multilateral instrument (data trusts, attestation consortia, certification councils) stalled at its signatories. All principal combatants exited profitable: Blue on appeals recovery and collected contract paper, Red on rotated technical yield and stabilized retention, Green on invoiced (if partially starved) clawbacks and a defensible fiduciary file, the Vendor on a partial exit. Nothing is settled; the three-year locks, the unbuilt technical counter-corpus, and the deferred fee-economics renegotiation all point the same conflict into the 2031-32 renewal cycle with sharper tools on every side.
rapporteur.endStateName: Quiet-Front Attrition: a member-invisible, contract-governed war of profitable escalation
keyDynamics: Referee absence as physics: the W2 environment absorbed nearly all legal-theater investment (stripped statute, CMS forbearance, standing dismissals), making bilateral private ordering the only rulebook that actually operated before 2030.

Hydraulic yield displacement: every time an adverse-action channel was constrained (clawback riders, corpus-driven CD parity on clinical documentation), recovery pressure reappeared within one turn in an unconstrained channel (post-pay ASO, then COB/DRG/itemized-bill technical domains).

Proxy-keyed enforcement invites proxy starvation: Green's entire enforcement stack (clawbacks, appeal-bot sensors) keyed on overturns, so Red defeated it by producing recoveries with single-digit overturn rates rather than fewer recoveries.

Concession as weapon: Red repeatedly surrendered terms that cost nothing (transparency, audit, even clawbacks) to purchase things that mattered (three-year locks past scoring, retention stabilization, regulatory oxygen), converting adversary leverage peaks into locked ground.

Two-speed diffusion: bilateral commercial paper (riders, repricing amendments, RFP exhibits) spread at procurement speed across three channels, while every multilateral instrument (Data Trust, Attestation Consortium, Certification Council) stayed frozen at table-actor signatures for three straight turns, exactly on base rate.

Scored-metric shielding: Red escalated exclusively where nothing was measured - member-invisible surfaces, and MA post-pay expansion timed to the 2029 Stars measure sunset - demonstrating that measurement perimeters, not statutes, set the escalation map.
The capability-diffusion (CD) recompute race, not any legal event, governed who captured the largest contested dollar pool each turn (4 to ~2 to a rotated 3).
criticalJunctures: Turn 1: the W2 environment absorbs both sides' seeded legal-primary theater (one stripped statute, CMS forbearance) - the game's economics permanently relocate to private contract and capability channels.

Turn 1: Green fires carrier-affiliated PI off its five anchor books inside the turn - the first binding constraint on Red PI behavior anywhere in the game, arriving through the employer channel with no renewal lag, before any statute or court acts.

Turn 2: NationalCo preemptively concedes the no-clawback line inside a retention rider traded for three-year locks and pared-back exclusivity - Green banks economics but loses its market test, and its leverage window closes until 2031.

Turn 2: the Data Trust corpus goes to production at Meridian and White recomputes the post-pay documentation CD gap from ~4 to ~2 - capping Red's clinical capture band and setting up the Turn 3 rotation.
Turn 2: the all-lines-of-business clause dies at the Lakeview renewal table - the ERISA/ASO perimeter Red drew holds through final scoring, confining Blue's rider to fully-insured volume.

Turn 3: Red's yield rotation into clawback-immune, low-overturn technical domains (adjudicated at CD 3) - the single move that decided the endgame, starving Green's reconciliation engine and the patient-AI sensor simultaneously while improving Green's own net-spend line.

Turn 3: NationalCo settles the surviving CAA count on Green's own published template - closing the only discovery channel that could reach PI-targeting documents before 2030 and decrementing the accrued litigation-shock clock.

registryScores.evidence: The displacement mechanism fired unambiguously in this D2xW2 cell, twice. When the Data Trust corpus recompute (CD 4 to ~2, T2) constrained Red's clinical-documentation capture band, and Green's signed clawback/cap riders constrained overturn-generating recoveries, Red's yield reappeared within one turn in non-denial adverse-action channels: COB, itemized-bill, DRG-validation and credit-balance audits, adjudicated at CD 3 and booked as fee revenue inside Green's caps (T3). Red PI yield ended improving_moderate despite the constraints; the media record notes a hospital-facing technical-audit surge. Caveat: the White Cell dollar ledger needed to compute a numeric displacement ratio was not published in this record, so the >=0.33 threshold is inferred from the qualitative and state-variable record, not calculated.

The channel-shift rider is supported: every weaponization of a published artifact ran through non-regulatory channels (negotiation, procurement, media), never through a regulator. The Vendor's sworn conflict certification was cited adversely three times (Green's for-cause termination T2, Blue's contingency-master repricing T2, exit-multiple discount T3); the two-tier paper record was used in Green's parity squeeze (T3); the T1 lobbying filings and T2/T3 media cycles entered the permanent citable record. Lag matched the W2 prediction (1-2 turns). However, the strong claim that <50% of published artifacts remain cost-free fails on this record: Green's benchmarking utility, its published settlement term sheet (which Red signed on terms favorable to Red, but which delivered Green's settlement), Blue's DUA-based experience reports, and the executed rider paper all reached end-game without adverse citation against their publishers.

The discriminating test requires a per-turn Blue cost ledger (appeal ops + prevention + governance + audit + arbitration) and denial-volume counts to compute cost-per-denial; no such dollar ledger appears in this game's published record. Qualitatively consistent tolls are visible (contingency funding structures, the LTIP retention pool as a 'fixed insurance cost', SLA-interest administration, annual barrier re-audits), but neither the $65/$80 thresholds nor the volume-cost correlation can be scored from this record.

Red never de-escalated from cost pain in this D2xW2 game, and its self-funded PI activity was explicitly fee-revenue-positive throughout ('nearly pure-margin fee revenue', PI yield improving in all three turns, MLR-exempt by design). Every Red concession has a coded external trigger: pre-service PA restraint in MA was Stars-measurement-driven (and expanded the moment the measures sunset in 2029); the jumbo retention rider and clawback concession were triggered by employer abrasion (retention was the scored soft spot after Green fired carrier-affiliated PI); the T3 CAA settlement was triggered by litigation discovery risk. Zero cost-exhaustion triggers appear anywhere in the adjudication record.

This D2xW2 game did not converge to a comprehensive detente: escalation ended elevated, the contest continued on rotated technical surfaces, and the end-state is grinding-contest-with-a-contract-layer, not armistice. Both halves of the instrument claim held exactly: no numeric denial-rate corridor was signed, proposed at any table, or even survived legislative committee (the Vendor/Red pen stripped corridor language in T1; White's signability gate never saw corridor paper); every signed instrument in three turns of signability rulings is a process term (disclosure, SLAs with interest, gold-carding criteria, audit rights, fee/clawback compensation terms). One game cannot establish the <33% F2-primary rate for the cell, but this game is a clean data point in the predicted direction.

No Blue actor published an AI-governance charter, and no publisher-vs-internal-governor pairing existed; no SIU-audit or qui-tam events were adjudicated against any Blue actor. The nearest analog runs through other cells: the Vendor's published sworn conflict certification became its most damaging exposure (for-cause termination, repricing leverage, exit discount), and Red's attestation standard drew an Allied Tube conversion - both directionally consistent with 'publication is the exposure vector' - but neither constitutes the hypothesis's specified test.

Zero adjudicated distress events (distress sale, exclusive-terms delegation capture, PE acquisition) occurred in any provider tier across three turns; Blue closed with margins improving and three of four metrics up. The record contains only precursors: Prairie locked on 2026 paper with cost-raising dispute-ladder/record-standard clauses through 2029 (a diffusion block, not distress), and a T3 media cycle about thin-margin hospitals facing algorithmic nickel-and-dime audits. With no distress events on either side of the comparison, the 2x mid-tier-vs-rural rate claim cannot be scored from this game.

Binding instruments distributed contract-by-contract across all three turns with no synchronized window: 2026-27 (Prairie lock, Red jumbo transparency riders, Vendor masters), 2028 (Lakeview subset rider, GovProgramCo bilateral, NationalCo retention rider, Aligned Integrity conversions), 2029-30 (CAA settlement, episode-access rider, legacy-fleet conversion, gold-carding expansion) - no single year plausibly holds >25-40% of them. First-cycle wins were wedge provisions exactly as predicted: the Lakeview rider bound only a disclosure/SLA/gold-carding subset on fully-insured lines; full economics (Green's caps and clawbacks) bound only in cycle two, and the deeper renegotiation (gross-recovery triggers) was explicitly deferred past 2030. The escalation index stayed elevated through the final turn, with Red's largest-intensity move (technical-domain rotation plus post-Stars MA post-pay expansion) landing in 2029-30 - the late peak the D2 rider predicts.

This is one game of the decisive D2xW2 cell and it is plausibly codable as grinding-escalation-primary: no detente formed, escalation stayed elevated through scoring, Red's endgame was continued escalation (rotated, member-invisible), and the conflict rolls unresolved into 2031-32. That is directionally consistent with the claim that D1 doctrine, not strategic logic, suppressed this end-state in Study 1. But the grind here is unusually profitable and paper-managed (a sustained process-term floor, a settlement, mutual metric improvement), so classification between 'grinding uncoordinated escalation' and 'contest with cooperative edges' is genuinely contestable, and the >=40%-of-games frequency criterion cannot be evaluated with n=1.

Partial coverage, supportive where testable. Robust strategies that ran at scale were non-negative in this cell: renewal loading (Lakeview rider subset signed and cashed via SLA interest), BATNA-first (Lakeview declining early renewal converted the 2028 renewal into a leverage event; direct-contract pilots priced the exit), and recovery-side operations (the 40% engine, the game's cleanest ledger all three turns). The predicted D2 exception also has evidence: asymmetric recovery escalation - the appeal-factory family - was locally winning in D2xW2, and Red's escalation-behind-a-shield was P&L-positive throughout. Fragile-side: weaponized transparency underperformed (dossier/legislative spend largely absorbed by W2; Blue itself retargeted legal spend after T1), and corridors were never attempted. But governance-seat occupation and upcoding inoculation were never committed at the >=40-posture-point threshold, so the full table cannot be scored.

In this GREEN-active W2 game the first event that measurably curtailed Red PI behavior on self-funded volume was unambiguously the employer channel: Green fired carrier-affiliated PI off five anchor books inside Turn 1 (explicitly 'no renewal lag on that lever'), and Red's T2 concessions (fee caps, overturn clawbacks, transparency riders) were adjudicated as responses to the scored retention vulnerability - while the statutory channel never bound at all (stripped statute effective 2028 with attestation-grade compliance; CMS forbearance; regulator described as reactive throughout). Contagion also ran faster commercially: rider terms reached the Vendor's converted fleet and Red's voluntary mid-market offering via RFP/consultant channels while two statehouses adjourned three consecutive years. Caveats: no GREEN-inactive control exists in this game, and T3 showed the brake is partially escapable - Red rotated around the overturn-keyed clawback mechanics rather than reducing PI intensity.

The arms-dealer mechanism left clear causal traces, but both designed comparisons are unavailable. Supportive: the Vendor's T1 talent raid slipped Meridian's self-build ~2 quarters, extending Blue's dependence; its drafting pen stripped the one enacted statute of volume-shrinking terms while its model-bill campaign explicitly targeted 'kill corridors, sell compliance'; it sold ammunition to all four other cells simultaneously and its stated T3 objective was keeping disputed-dollar volume high through scoring. Not testable: no VENDOR-inactive same-seed run exists for the duration/prevention-adoption comparison, and the scripted payer-acquisition inject never fired (the Vendor instead split itself and sold the denial-defense arm; the PI arm was unsold at scoring), so the data-rights/protection differential cannot be scored.

This is a W2 game and the federal preemption shock seed did not fire; the hypothesis's comparison set is preemption-seeded vs control within W3 cells. Background ERISA preemption operated throughout as existing law (it confined every state-channel and rider gain to fully-insured volume), which is consistent with the hypothesis's premise that private ordering dominates where the state channel is absent, but the discriminating inject-vs-control test is unavailable here.

No priced provider-asset acquisition moves appear in this game's record, and nothing indicates the acquisition mechanic was enabled in this cell. Red's observed responses to constrained denial channels were rotation (into technical domains) and negotiation (retention riders, settlement), plus capability in-sourcing from the Vendor - but absent evidence that acquisition was available and priced, this cannot be read as Red preferring non-acquisition. The one live thread is post-horizon: the unsold Vendor PI arm's possible sale to 'a rival carrier's services arm' is flagged as a 2031 signpost, not an in-game event.

The floor held decisively in this game, in one of the hypothesis's stress-adjacent cells (D2xW2). Multiple bilateral process-term instruments from the payer-signable set were signed and sustained to end-game: the RegionalMutual-Lakeview rider subset (algorithm disclosure, escalation SLAs with interest actually invoiced and collected in T3, criteria-based gold-carding); the GovProgramCo-Meridian/Summit gold-carding and API-conformance bilateral (signed T2, expanded by amendment T3, cited by CMS as an implementation showcase); and Red's jumbo ASO transparency/audit riders from T1. Process substance additionally diffused through channels no one compelled - RegionalMutual's voluntary mid-market ASO offering and the Vendor's converted fleet - while the same tables struck every attempt at broader reach (all-lines clause) and no corridor was ever proposed. The floor coexisted with elevated escalation throughout, exactly as the 'floor, not modal end-state' framing predicts.

cellAssessments.blue: Blue's seeded legal-primary strategy failed on contact with W2 (one stripped statute, CMS forbearance) but its Turn-1 hedge became the franchise: the never-resubmitted-40% appeals engine was the cleanest ledger on the board all three turns, contingency-funded and scaled coalition-wide, while the Data Trust delivered a genuine CD recompute (4 to ~2) that capped Red's clinical capture band. Blue closed with leakage improving moderately and three of four metrics up, plus signed, cash-generating rider paper (SLA interest, gold-carding). Its two structural failures define its 2031 exposure: the all-lines clause died at every table, leaving ASO volume - the game's largest dollar pool - outside every instrument it built; and its clinical corpus is useless against Red's technical-domain rotation, for which it has no matured counter before 2031.
cellAssessments.red: The game's best performer. Red read both the world and the paper more carefully than anyone: it let W2 do its regulatory work for free (preemption shield mostly bought what the environment was giving away), spent concessions only where they were cheap (transparency, audit, even clawbacks) to purchase things that were dear (three-year locks past scoring, retention stabilization, Stars quiet), and executed the endgame's decisive maneuver - rotating matured, in-sourced PI capacity into clawback-immune, low-overturn, member-invisible technical domains timed to the Stars measure sunset. It bought down its one pre-2030 tail risk with a narrow settlement on the plaintiff's own template. All four scored metrics closed defensible; costs: a real fee-yield haircut, transparency substance now irreversibly in the market, and an accrued-but-undischarged litigation clock (Lokken) plus a discoverable off-paper Lakeview linkage waiting past the horizon.
cellAssessments.green: Green built exceptional leverage and learned that winning terms is not realizing them. Its employer channel was the first and only binding constraint on Red PI in the entire game (anchor-book PI firings, T1) and it banked the economics two years of pressure created - caps, clawbacks, audit rights, a settled CAA count on its own template, a completed market test, and the game's cleanest fiduciary file. But it paid in three-year locks that closed its pressure window until 2031, and its entire enforcement architecture keyed on overturns, which Red then stopped producing: the reconciliation engine was starved by the same rotation that (ironically) improved Green's net-spend line, since technical recoveries return sponsor money. Green exits with improved spend, low fiduciary exposure, and a deferred fee-economics fight it must re-arm for.
cellAssessments.vendor: The classic arsonist-and-fire-brigade arc, compressed. Turn 1's only unambiguous winner (ARR improving_large, both-sides contingency positions, the statute diluted by its own pen), it spent the rest of the game paying for the model's discoverability: the sworn conflict certification it signed for revenue became the most weaponized document on the board - a for-cause termination, repricing leverage for Blue, parity concessions for Green, and an exit-multiple discount. Its structural responses (Project Prenup, fleet-wide conversion to reformed terms, the Cleave split) cured exposure prospectively only; the 2026-27 record traveled with the holdco into escrow. It closed with ARR still growing slowly, the denial-defense arm sold inside the window, and the PI arm - its wholesale channel eaten by NationalCo's in-sourcing - unsold at scoring. Its most durable legacy is unintentional: its bilateral paper was the fastest-diffusing instrument class in the game, and its converted fleet became a major diffusion channel for Green's terms.

surprises: Concession as the turn-winning weapon: NationalCo preemptively surrendered the no-clawback line that had defined Turn 1 - the confrontation Green built two years of leverage for never happened, and the concession purchased three-year locks that neutralized Green through final scoring.

The clawback regime was defeated by arithmetic, not defiance: because every enforcement mechanism keyed on overturns, Red honored every signed instrument while rotating into single-digit-overturn technical domains - full compliance and full escalation simultaneously.

Green's net spend improved because of Red's escalation: technical recoveries on ASO volume are sponsor money returned, so the same maneuver that starved Green's enforcement engine flattered its scored outcome.

Patient appeal-bots became, unintentionally, Green's fee-enforcement sensors (bot-won overturns mechanically triggered contractual clawbacks) - and were then structurally starved by Red's rotation before they mattered.

Blue's rider substance diffused through Red's own sales force: RegionalMutual voluntarily sold transparency dashboards and capped fees as a mid-market ASO differentiator - the compelled instrument failed while its content spread as a competitive weapon.

The single most consequential document in the game was a procurement exhibit: the Vendor's sworn conflict-of-interest certification generated more realized leverage across more cells than any statute, court ruling, or multilateral standard.

The seeded primary theater (legislation and regulation) was the game's worst investment for both coalitions, while the highest-ROI move on the board was the least glamorous: industrializing appeals on denials nobody had bothered to contest.

frictionViolations.rule: Contract terms bind only at renewal (earliest broad effect Turn 2)
frictionViolations.violation: Green terminates carrier-affiliated PI arrangements on five anchor books mid-turn, with the adjudicator asserting 'no renewal lag on that lever' by fiat. Green's charter does allow firing PI vendors independent of the carrier, and services contracts often carry termination-for-convenience clauses, but the record never establishes that contractual basis — the renewal-friction waiver is asserted, not adjudicated.

frictionViolations.rule: IT/AI deployments take 12-24 months to measurable impact
frictionViolations.violation: NationalCo's frontier-model post-pay escalation is credited with 'capturing the majority of the contested swing durably' and booked fee revenue inside the same turn it launched. Defensible because the archetype carries pre-existing frontier automation (scaling, not new build), and the 18-month turn gives cover, but the immediate 'durable' capture compresses the deployment-to-impact lag to near zero.

frictionViolations.rule: IT/AI deployments take 12-24 months to measurable impact
frictionViolations.violation: Red's Yield Rotation into COB, itemized-bill, DRG-validation and credit-balance domains is scored at CD gap 3 with durable-band capture within the same turn. The in-sourced stack's maturation was correctly clocked (T2 start, T3 maturity), but re-targeting a clinical-medical-necessity stack into distinct technical-recovery domains is treated as instantaneous; real new-domain model capability would consume a meaningful fraction of a deployment window. Partially mitigated by the fact that COB/itemized audit is a mature rules-based domain.

Narrative credits GovProgramCo gold-carding expansion with having 'deleted disputed volume outright' — stronger language than the bounded, low-coverage effect the game's own milestone ledger records (single-digit-to-<20% of PA volume, meaningful relief 2030+). The ledger holds the line; the prose overshoots it.

baseRateViolations.expected: Contract-language diffusion base rate: new terms class reaches majority of agreements in 10-15 yrs organically, 5-7 yrs if statutorily forced
baseRateViolations.observed: Record repeatedly cites a '3-7 yr contract-language base rate' (T2 and T3 diffusion ledgers) — a band 2 years more lenient than the table's forced-diffusion floor. Outcomes remained conservative (nothing reached majority by 2030), so the mis-cite did not distort scoring, but the stated anchor is wrong.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 spec: 85-90% of suits settle quietly, confidential, cash-only, NO process commitments; base-rate settlement window yrs 4-7 (behavioral/operational effects possible ~2 yrs in at discovery stage)
baseRateViolations.observed: The NationalCo-Green CAA settlement lands ~2.5 yrs from filing and includes structural data access, retrospective fee credits, and audit cooperation — a process-laden, faster-than-modal outcome. Within the 10-15% non-modal allowance and consistent with the table's note that operational effects precede legal resolution, and it was player-purchased rather than environment-granted — but it is the optimistic edge of the distribution presented as the game's one litigation payoff.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 patient-AI endpoint: 2% growing to 8-10% of appeals by game end
baseRateViolations.observed: Appeal-bot share ends at 'roughly 6-8%,' described as 'the top of the W2 endpoint band.' The value is actually at or below the band floor and the label is wrong; deviation is in the conservative direction and per-turn stepping (2-3% → 4-5% → 6-8%) is smooth and spec-shaped.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 spec: state AI-UR laws pass in 4-8 states over the whole game
baseRateViolations.observed: Exactly 1 statute enacts across all three turns (with two target states adjourning three consecutive times); the T1 bulletin calls one enactment 'consistent with W2's 4-8-states-per-game ceiling,' treating a range as a pure ceiling. Ambiguity about off-screen non-player states gives partial cover, but as written the environment under-delivers the spec's own statute band, overstating regulatory emptiness.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 media flare frequency 1-in-2 per turn
baseRateViolations.observed: Media roll hit in all three turns (12.5% likelihood on fair rolls). Not a rule violation — dice can do this, and each flare correctly decayed in one cycle with roughly symmetric targeting — but the streak is worth noting for calibration of 'the paper trail accumulates' findings.

audit.worldModelFidelity: High fidelity to W2 in substance, with one structural caveat. Substance: CMS behavior (attestation-based good-faith discretion, extensions through 2028-29, teeth deferred past horizon) matches the W2 spec and the 0057-F base-rate row almost verbatim; the one enacted statute followed the full lag table (effective +2 yrs, symbolic year-1 compliance, single-digit fine in year 2, behavior change 2031-33, patch-bill flagged as modal route); voluntary standards (Red Attestation Consortium, Vendor Certification Council) were correctly held immature per the Da Vinci base rate across all three turns; gold-carding stayed inside the single-digit-to-<20% coverage band in the ledgers; non-player employers stayed inertial per GREEN-passive rules, with diffusion only via evidence and bilateral paper; courts produced no precedent, class-cert stayed beyond horizon, and the Lokken clock tracked the real-world litigation table; no rescue event ever arrived, which is exactly W2's design function. Deviations: (1) the game ran 3 turns of ~18 months against the ensemble spec's 8-10 turns of ~6 months — the Common Rules' own 18-month-turn language (§3.1) creates a genuine spec conflict, but applying W2's per-6-month-turn event frequencies to 18-month turns cut environment event density roughly 3x, biasing the world even quieter than W2 intends; (2) only 1 statute vs the spec's 4-8-state band; (3) one settlement carried process terms against the cash-only modal; (4) patient-AI ended slightly under band while being labeled top-of-band. All deviations except the settlement run in the conservative/quieter direction, reinforcing rather than contradicting W2's null-hypothesis role.
downweightRecommendations: Down-weight the Turn 3 lesson that clawback/overturn-keyed enforcement paper is trivially evaded by same-turn domain rotation: Red's instant CD-3 capture in COB/DRG/itemized-bill domains compressed a realistic 6-18 month capability build to zero, so in reality Green's clawback regime would bite for longer before the rotation completed. The directional insight (enforcement mechanisms keyed on overturns are gameable) stands; the speed and cleanliness of the evasion should not be cited as calibrated.

Treat the CAA litigation-as-crowbar payoff (structural data-access settlement at ~2.5 years) as the optimistic tail of the W2 settlement distribution, not a repeatable template: the world spec's modal outcome is confidential cash-only settlement, and the record itself said so at Turn 1 before delivering the non-modal result.

Discount conclusions of the form 'the referee-state stayed home' or 'the environment never showed up' by one notch: the 18-month-turn compression applied W2 per-turn event frequencies at roughly one-third the spec's density, and only 1 statute enacted against the spec's 4-8-state band, so the game's environment was quieter than even W2 prescribes.

Read all contract-diffusion timeline claims against the correct 5-7 yr (forced) / 10-15 yr (organic) bands, not the '3-7 yr' band the record cites; projections like 'majority of ASO agreements 2032-34' should be treated as the earliest plausible edge rather than the central estimate.

Findings that survived intact and deserve full weight: the appeals-yield/never-resubmitted-40% economics (ledger-positive, friction-respecting, bounded every turn), the multilateral-instrument futility pattern (every standard/consortium held immature exactly per base rates), the bilateral-paper-diffuses-fastest finding, and the fully-insured/ASO perimeter holding against the Transparency Rider — all are base-rate-clean.

games.name: Asymmetric Squeeze
games.seed: Market context: highly consolidated payers, fragmented providers. Prairie (rural) and Summit (physician enterprise) carry heavy prior-auth burden and cannot resource AI. Meridian can self-build; Lakeview is capital-constrained with 45% single-payer concentration. Red opens with aggressive automated adjudication concentrated where resistance is weakest. Green is largely absent from small-provider geographies. Vendor is pitching subsidized denial-defense to the small tier.

turns.narrative: Turn 1 closes with the contest asymmetric by design and asymmetric in result. NationalCo's pre-pay yield engine hit the small tier exactly where the capability arithmetic said it would: frontier models, full claims history, and audit-consent paper against providers fielding, at best, a contingency appeal-letter tool that went live in the back half of the turn. On the contested small-tier ASO volume the capability gap exceeds three points and Red captures the majority of the swing — booked as services-arm fee revenue, durable under doctrine until Blue's data pool matures. But Red also gave ground deliberately: GovProgramCo's loud 0057-F compliance and front-end MA retreat shrank the very denial classes Blue and Vendor had targeted for the 80-percent-overturn arbitrage. The appeals machine Prairie and Summit switched on found a smaller pool of easy wins than their move sheets assumed, and the growing dispute class — DRG downgrades and itemized-bill edits — is a documentation fight their letter-generators handle poorly. The environment did almost nothing to help anyone. No statute moved. CMS restated the January 2027 deadline in an FAQ that trade press read, correctly, as flexibility. A rural-distress story flared regionally and died against RegionalMutual's Fast Pass announcement. Patient-side appeal AI stayed a niche curiosity. The turn's real action was paper: RegionalMutual signed its amendment package at Lakeview and Prairie with modest process concessions bought cheap; NationalCo got its Transparency Charter onto a handful of jumbo accounts before Green's rider could bind, splitting Green's coalition at the margin exactly as the defection test predicted; Green issued its rider anyway and signed a below-network Summit pilot term sheet, making the churn threat real at pilot scale. Vendor grew on both sides of the fight, lost the Sentinel flank to Green's conflict screen, and bought itself a discoverable hypocrisy file lobbying against the gold cards it sells relief from. Meridian executed its capability turn as promised — board approval, BDIX chartered in converted form, formation costs sunk — but lost a key rev-cycle lead to the raid and a quarter or two of schedule with it. Nothing scored large this turn; nearly everything scored durable. Turn 2 is when the signed paper binds, the audits report, and the question resolves whether Blue's pooled-data leapfrog can recompute the differential before Red's fee engine compounds out of reach.
env: CMS (W2 posture): sub-regulatory FAQ restates the January 2027 CMS-0057-F API deadline while emphasizing 'good-faith implementation' will inform enforcement posture — trade press reads it as early flexibility signaling; general media ignores it. WEDI-pattern readiness surveys suggest 30-50% of obligated payers will not be fully ready at the compliance date.

Courts (background clocks, no new consequential ruling this turn): Lokken discovery into AI claims processes grinds forward on its pre-existing schedule; one copycat algorithmic-denial suit filed against a national payer, with a motion-to-dismiss ruling not expected for 12-18 months and quiet cash settlement the modal W2 outcome. NationalCo's non-solicit action against the Vendor holding entity joins the slow queue.

Media (1-turn flare, decays): regional outlets run a 'rural hospital squeezed by automated bill audits' story anchored on a Prairie-like facility's losses; RegionalMutual's same-week Fast Pass gold-card launch supplies the counter-narrative and the story fails to nationalize. Coverage decays next turn absent a fresh shock.

Patient-side appeal AI: no milestone this turn — usage holds at roughly 2-3% of adverse determinations, concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members; no statutory tailwind under the prevailing deregulatory federal posture.

State legislatures: several SB 1120-style AI-UR bills carry over or die in committee; no player-relevant state enacts new UM law this turn. Gold-card statute amendments remain narrow, consistent with weak-uptake findings.

Labor market: senior SIU, clinical-audit, and rev-cycle analytics talent is bid up sharply by PE equity packages; White notes error-rate risk for any actor backfilling raided functions with junior staff on compressed timelines.

sign.instrument: BDIX Charter and Data Contribution Agreement (Blue)
sign.detail: Pooled denial observatory among competitor providers is checklist item 4 post-safety-zone-withdrawal exposure. Converted: independent third-party manager (not Meridian), aggregated and de-identified outputs with a 3-month historical lag, no participant access to rivals' disaggregated data, express bar on rate/contracting-strategy fields. Payer-response-latency and adjudication-behavior fields survive. Conversion adds formation cost and lead time, booked to Blue's ledger.

sign.instrument: Lakeview–RegionalMutual Renewal Process Rider (Blue)
sign.detail: Automation disclosure, escalation SLAs, timely-filing tolling, symmetric audit rights, gold-card criteria are all checklist items 6-11. Signed only in diluted hybrid form after negotiation; full auto-pend-on-breach did not survive counterparty leverage. No corridor content proposed.

sign.instrument: Coalition Vendor MSA with Conflict Firewall (Blue)
sign.detail: Ordinary bilateral commercial terms: contingency pricing, data-use restrictions, audit rights, liquidated damages, termination for convenience. Firewall breach is enforceable and, per White's Vendor rule, independently discoverable.

sign.instrument: ASO Transparency & Recovery Charter (Red/NationalCo)
sign.detail: Data access, capped contingency fees, audit rights, reporting — process terms bundled with a 3-year term. Signable as-is; note Charter definitions of 'recovery' and audit scope are payer-drafted, a fact Green's T2 audit may contest.

sign.instrument: Fast Pass Gold-Card Protocol (Red/RegionalMutual)
sign.detail: Checklist item 9; statutorily blessed model. Published criteria, requalification, continuity-of-care protection. Base rate warns uptake runs single-digit percent of providers in years 1-3.

sign.instrument: Participation Amendment Package (Red/RegionalMutual)
sign.detail: Audit consent, policy-manual incorporation by reference with 60-day change notice (meets item 7 notice floor), corrected-claim filing windows, internal escalation SLAs. Signable; filing-window terms remain subject to state prompt-pay statutes on the fully-insured book and bind ASO volume only as contract terms.

sign.instrument: Fiduciary Data & Fee Rider (Green)
sign.detail: Line-level data access, fee cap with flat-fee conversion, 100% clawback on reversed recoveries, purchaser-selected auditor, termination for data breach — all process terms between plan sponsor and TPA; no corridor content. Reversal clawback is a fee term, not a denial quota. Survives the gate as drafted.

sign.instrument: Coalition PI Vendor Conflict-Disclosure Standard (Green)
sign.detail: Purchasing-side certification precondition among non-competing buyers of administrative services; low antitrust exposure. Effective this turn: it disqualified the duopoly's Sentinel bid.

sign.instrument: Direct-Contract Pilot Term Sheet (Green–Summit/Meridian)
sign.detail: Bilateral prospective-payment and employer-granted gold-carding terms; no gate issues. Scale claims struck to pilot scope per Rules 3.2.

turns.bluePosture: Asymmetric arbitrage, not symmetric escalation. Blue's Turn 1 thesis: the single most valuable fact in the environment is the appeal-economics gap — 80.7% of MA prior-auth appeals were fully or partially overturned in 2024 while only 1.6–19.9% of denials were ever appealed. That is a massive pool of recoverable revenue that requires no denial-rate corridor, no litigation win, and no symmetric AI arms race to capture: it requires appeal VOLUME at low unit cost, concentrated exactly where Red is concentrating automated adjudication (Prairie, Summit). So Blue spends T1 doing three things: (1) industrializing cheap, high-volume appeals against the highest-overturn denial classes coalition-wide; (2) building the one durable CD asset small providers can never buy alone — pooled cross-payer denial-behavior data (the D2 capability-leapfrog channel) — anchored on Meridian's balance sheet; (3) converting Lakeview's single renewal window into signable process terms (transparency, SLAs, tolling, audit rights) rather than a rate war it cannot survive. We accept that almost nothing pays this turn (12–24 mo IT lag, renewal friction); T1 is deliberately a capability-and-contract turn positioned so T2 deltas land inside bounded-movement limits from a defensible base. We defend the small tier now with bought tools on coalition-negotiated terms, because a Prairie collapse degrades Blue's data pool, Blue's margin scorecard, and Lakeview/Meridian's rural referral economics.

turns.narrative: Turn 2 belonged to whoever had already signed something. The award season Green engineered in T1 produced the turn's structural event: RegionalMutual, offered the accounts defecting from NationalCo, ran the defection math White's doctrine requires and signed the Fiduciary Data & Fee Rider substantially as drafted for a mid-market tranche — the first carrier signature, clearing the pre-declared piloted threshold. NationalCo's Charter 2.0 did its job where it mattered most, locking the jumbo book behind fee caps and three-year terms, but the definitional contest is no longer a contest between drafts; one standard now has a carrier's ink and audit findings behind it. Those findings were the audit's real yield: the purchaser-selected auditor documented contingency fees retained on recoveries later reversed — arithmetic guaranteed by the overturn base rates — and NationalCo settled into its 50%-plus-credit posture rather than litigate its own definitions during RFP season. On the capability front, D2 physics cut both ways. NationalCo's second-generation engine and sub-90-day edit rotation kept the small-tier gap at three-plus and left BDIX publishing portraits of retired edit postures; fee revenue compounded on undefended volume and RegionalMutual's licensed book. But on Meridian's own claims the differential narrowed to two: documentation origination is a data-access advantage no audit engine can replicate, and downgrade sustain rates on packet-defended claims bent Blue's way late in the turn — coalition-wide effect waits on the 12-to-24-month deployment clock. GovProgramCo ran its calendar arbitrage without a wobble: loose MA front end, attestation shield live, re-tightening playbook staged for the year the Stars measures stop counting. Prairie's exit from the Shield contingency trap and the signed rural wraparound removed disputes rather than defending them — pilot-scale, but the one move no capability differential touches. Vendor stemmed Shield churn with floor guarantees, sold defensible automation to GovProgramCo after RegionalMutual's incumbent stack blocked the parity pitch, and then undercut its own Clearline independence play by that same sale — a collision White records as a discoverable fact. The environment stayed molasses: the January 2027 API deadline passed on attestations, one more state enacted a clinician-determination statute that cannot bite in-game, a Lokken discovery filing leaked one uncomfortable throughput metric, and patient-side appeal AI crept to roughly four percent. Escalation remains rational for Red, retention is now visibly priced, and Turn 3 turns on whether Blue's packet layer reaches coalition scale before the fee engine finishes compounding.
env: CMS: the January 2027 CMS-0057-F compliance date passed inside this window with attestation-based enforcement — no corrective-action plans issued, no penalties; a WEDI-pattern follow-up survey finds roughly 40% of obligated payers with partial or non-functional prior-auth APIs. Trade press covers it; general media does not.

Courts: a partially unsealed Lokken discovery filing references internal post-acute review throughput metrics, generating one turn of trade and regional coverage without a ruling; the T1 copycat suit's motion to dismiss remains pending on its 12-18 month clock; the NationalCo-Vendor non-solicit action exits the queue via confidential settlement; Green's newly filed ERISA fiduciary action docketed with no in-turn activity.

State legislatures: one additional player-relevant state enacts an SB 1120-pattern clinician-determination statute — the fifth such regime nationally; effective date lags and audit-driven enforcement mean no in-game bite, but it validates attestation-layer compliance postures and marginally strengthens documentation-based provider positions.

Media (1-turn flare, decays): an employer-benefits trade story on the Green coalition audit — carriers keeping contingency fees on recoveries later reversed — runs for one cycle and fails to nationalize; no counter-flare on rural audits materializes because Prairie's shift to prospective payment removed the distress anchor.

Patient-side appeal AI: modest milestone — usage ticks from 2-3% to roughly 4% of adverse determinations on the strength of consumer appeal-bot coverage, still concentrated among commercially insured high-literacy members; Red's migration of recovery activity to member-invisible post-pay surfaces suppresses the fuel supply, as designed.

Labor market: PE bidding pressure on SIU and rev-cycle talent cools at the margin as the settlement's mutual 24-month non-solicit sidelines the most aggressive raider on named roles; Meridian's junior-backfill error-rate risk persists through the first half of the turn before senior pairing stabilizes packet quality.

DOL: Green's referral opens a routine inquiry into TPA compensation disclosure; W2 posture makes closure without action the modal outcome, but the open file is citable in RFP negotiations while it lasts.

turns.bluePosture: Capability-leapfrog on defensible terrain. Turn 1 proved Blue cannot win a CD contest against NationalCo's frontier pre-pay engine on generic claim edits — so Blue stops fighting there. Turn 2 redeploys the coalition onto the one domain where Blue holds the structural data advantage: the clinical record itself. The dispute mix Red chose (DRG downgrades, itemized-bill edits) is a documentation fight, and documentation originates on Blue's side of the wall. Meridian's self-build (chartered T1, inside the 12-24 month window) matures into evidence-at-source defense; BDIX's converted-form observatory starts publishing payer-behavior latency data; Lakeview enforces paper it already signed rather than demanding new paper; Prairie exits the Vendor contingency trap into coalition shared services; Summit scales the Green direct-contract proof point that makes employer churn — Red's real vulnerability — credible. Simultaneously, Blue accepts every front-end de-escalation Red is selling (Fast Pass, PA retreat) at face value: taking the peace Red offers on prior auth is free margin and shrinks Vendor's dispute pool, not Blue's. The posture is asymmetric by design: fight where CD favors us, buy peace where it doesn't, and route the biggest lever — ASO account pressure — through Green.

turns.narrative: The scoring turn resolved through convergence rather than collision, and the last big dollars moved by signature. NationalCo bought its horizon — Charter 3.0 locked the jumbo book through 2031-32 — but Green dictated the price: discounted cash restitution of reversed-recovery fees, prospective 100% clawback parity, an independent recovery definition, and auditors the payer no longer nominates. The ERISA action was dismissed in the same closing; the DOL file shut without action a quarter later, its leverage already spent. On capability, Red declined the fight Blue had finally won. Meridian's origination layer reached full-clock maturity on its own book, and NationalCo rotated the fee engine off DRG clinical validation onto itemized-bill, COB, and repricing arithmetic — surfaces packets cannot read and where reversal rates are structurally too low for clawbacks to bite. Yield held flat instead of compounding; the concession was booked, not bled. GovProgramCo fired its two-turn calendar arbitrage the year the complaint and appeal measures left Stars, tightening post-pay, clinician-attested, member-invisible — one media cycle noted the timing and decayed on schedule. RegionalMutual finished as the market's certified clean carrier: rider across the full ASO book, contingency converted to subscription before Green's re-bid could take the work, Lakeview early-renewed on phased attachment-protocol paper that trades finality on qualified lines for two years of network stability. Lakeview wanted the full commercial book and got a schedule into 2031 — partial finality, honestly priced. Prairie ended the game never having fought: the wraparound went to full footprint and its disputes simply ceased to exist, the one outcome no capability differential touches. Summit's second cohort landed at roughly two-thirds of target, trimmed by the very renewal wave Green was monetizing on the other side of the table. Vendor cut itself in half on time — separation closed, the compliance entity under definitive agreement on a clean data room, the defense entity still in process at the bell, historical conflict facts discoverable forever. The environment stayed W2 to the end: a sixth clinician-determination statute that cannot bite in-game, the copycat suit settled for cash before its ruling, Lokken parked on a structured-resolution term sheet, patient appeal-AI drifting to roughly six percent. Final accounting: Blue's leakage bent moderately down on defended and removed volume; Red's trend, yield, retention, and Stars position all held or improved; Green converted paper into realized cash; Vendor exits half-sold at a recurring-revenue multiple. Nearly everyone ends better off than the drift line — because the disputed pool itself shrank, which is the quiet verdict of the game.
env: CMS: no enforcement event on 0057-F beyond attestation review, but API-transacted prior-auth volume becomes material on the standard 2-3-year post-deadline adoption curve — a background friction reduction for all providers, unowned by any player.

State legislatures: a sixth clinician-determination statute enacts in a player-relevant state; effective-date and audit-enforcement lags mean zero in-game bite, but it strengthens the market narrative for attestation layers and documentation-based positions.

Courts: the T1 copycat algorithmic-denial suit settles confidentially for cash before its motion-to-dismiss ruling — no admissions, no process terms, the W2 modal outcome. Lokken moves onto a structured-resolution term sheet; no further unsealing events this turn.
DOL: the TPA-compensation inquiry opened on Green's referral closes without action, after the Charter parity settlement had already extracted its negotiating value.

Media: one flare — a trade-press and single-regional-outlet cycle on GovProgramCo tightening post-pay audits the year complaint and appeal measures exited Stars scoring; the front-end PA retreat supplies the counter-narrative and the story fails to nationalize, decaying next cycle.

Patient-side appeal AI: drifts from roughly 4% to roughly 6% of adverse determinations, still concentrated among commercially insured high-literacy members; Red's migration of recovery activity to member-invisible post-pay surfaces continues to suppress fuel; no statutory tailwind.

Labor market: raiding pressure subsides — the T2 non-solicit settlement plus Cleave's 24-month cross-entity non-solicit calm the senior SIU/rev-cycle market; junior-backfill error-rate risk is no longer flagged for any table actor.

resolutions.move: Packet-at-Origination Coalition Scale-Out (Meridian to Lakeview/Summit; Prairie template)
resolutions.rationale: Meridian deployment satisfied the 12-24mo clock (live T2), scoring full effect on its own book; D2 leapfrog channel applies — origination data access recomputes CD prospectively, and sustain rates on defended DRG/downcoding classes move Blue's way. Lakeview/Summit score partial-turn effect only per the IT lag table, exactly as the self-limited move sheet claimed. Red's simultaneous rotation off clinical-validation surfaces concedes the contested class rather than paying run-rate to hold it.

resolutions.move: Lakeview 2029 Renewal: evidence-priced process terms
resolutions.rationale: Contract-repricing channel (1-3yr cycle) was open and both sides wanted paper: RegionalMutual's own retention move offered early renewal. Signed — but the attachment-protocol extension came phased (Fast Pass-qualified lines now, remaining commercial book on a 2030-31 schedule), finality limited to attached elements with T2 carve-outs, prompt-pay-parity interest accepted, two-year stability given. Full-book finality did not survive 45% counterparty leverage; the pre-drafted phased fallback executed.

resolutions.move: Dispute removal: Prairie wraparound PY2030 full footprint; Summit cohort 2
resolutions.rationale: Prairie leg succeeded in full — signed expansion within the 2-5pp/yr VBC ceiling, disputes on wraparound volume extinguished, stop-loss layering accepted. Summit cohort 2 landed at roughly two-thirds of target because NationalCo's Charter 3.0 early-renewal wave locked contested sponsors first, as Blue's own risk acceptance anticipated. Removed volume permanently exits Red's PI-eligible base.

resolutions.move: BDIX pivot to audit-grade retrospective evidence
resolutions.rationale: Concedes forward prediction (sub-90-day rotation beat it, per T2 record) and monetizes the demonstrated strength: renewal files priced the Lakeview negotiation, the Green license 2.0 is revenue-bearing, and the observatory ledger turns positive. Public report survives only in converted payer-de-identified form. Shock-probability contribution is real but lands beyond the horizon under D2's 3-7yr lag — no in-game scoring effect.

resolutions.move: NationalCo fee-engine mix rotation and PI platform licensing
resolutions.rationale: D2 arithmetic: hold the 3+ CD gap on arithmetic surfaces (itemized-bill, COB, repricing) where no origination advantage exists and reversal rates are structurally low, concede the surface where the gap closed to 2. Clawback drag on yield drops mechanically; PI yield holds flat against a shrinking disputed pool — a defensive success. Platform licensing signed first regional TPA licensees but recognizes only partial revenue inside the 12-24mo deployment window.

resolutions.move: GovProgramCo Stars-window re-tightening, post-pay and clinician-attested
resolutions.rationale: The economics brief is explicit that the 2029 Stars overhaul removes the complaints/appeals/disenrollment penalty; tooling was staged T2 so the deployment clock is satisfied. Post-pay surfaces do not trigger D2's customer-defection roll. Government-book trend improves within ±2pt bounded movement; the attestation stack keeps the algorithm-without-clinician theory factually unavailable. Costs booked: one media flare on the timing, elevated CMS program-audit exposure that cannot ripen before 2030 under W2.

resolutions.move: RegionalMutual clean-carrier retention play
resolutions.rationale: Retention was Red's only worsening indicator and this move reversed it: full-book rider extension, proactive flat-fee conversion that preempted Green's re-bid (right-to-match exercised), Lakeview early-renewed multi-year, Fast Pass widened only where sustain-rate data showed the yield already lost. Real price paid: contingency upside surrendered, audit yield in widened specialties gone permanently — margin concessions traded for scored retention.

resolutions.move: NationalCo shock-capping and Charter 3.0 horizon lock
resolutions.rationale: Copycat suit settled pre-MTD (W2 modal outcome) and the jumbo book is locked past the scoring horizon — both achieved. But Green's parity campaign set the toll: Charter 3.0 closed only bundled with restitution, 100% prospective clawback, and loss of the payer-nominated auditor panel. Lokken reached a structured-resolution term sheet, not a closing; its discovery clock is paused, not dead.

resolutions.move: Full-cycle clawback and flat-fee conversion on the rider book
resolutions.rationale: Pure contract-right exercise — no capability contest applies to enforcing signed terms, and the 80%+ overturn base rate made reversed-recovery fee retention arithmetically certain. Cash realized, conversion elections exercised, PI re-bid executed with RegionalMutual matching on most accounts and a conflict-certified independent taking a slice. Scored as realized recovery, not projection.

resolutions.move: Charter parity campaign converting ERISA action and DOL file
resolutions.rationale: Settlement was the only instrument that pays inside the game window (litigation clocks run 4-7yrs to resolution), and NationalCo's T2 posture had already revealed its preference for settling over defending its own definitions in RFP season. Restitution came discounted below full ask — as Green's own risk sheet priced — but parity terms, definitional replacement, and auditor independence all landed. The DOL closure without action arrived after its leverage had been converted, and the settlement file is a first-order CAA fiduciary-defensibility artifact.

resolutions.move: Direct-contract maturation: cohort 2, Prairie go-live, Meridian leg
resolutions.rationale: Prairie wraparound live at full footprint and the delayed Meridian high-dispute-line leg executed; cohort 2 trimmed to roughly two-thirds by Charter 3.0 lockups. Net-spend effect stays small-band per the VBC penetration ceiling, but the removed-dispute volume paid its second dividend as leverage in the clawback and parity negotiations, exactly as designed.

resolutions.move: Conflict-Disclosure Standard v2 and the Clearline line
resolutions.rationale: Purchasing-side certification passed the gate a third time; continuous PI-activity feeds and member-impact reporting close the visibility gap Red engineered by migrating to post-pay surfaces. Clearline recertification denied pending actual close of the Vendor separation — prospective-cure doctrine applied. External diffusion held to base rate: two prior external coalitions renewed on v2, nothing more claimed or granted.

resolutions.move: Project Cleave structural separation and dual exit processes
resolutions.rationale: Separation closed legally inside the 18-month window and the compliance entity reached a definitive agreement with a consolidator on a clean-book multiple, consistent with the evidence brief's PE transaction base rates. The defense entity remains in process at final scoring, and White rules the conflict cure prospective only — every T1-T2 ledger fact stays discoverable in both data rooms. Half an exit, honestly earned.

resolutions.move: Shield 3.0 DRG packet engine and contingency sunset
resolutions.rationale: The DRG suite narrows the small-tier CD gap on documentation classes — precisely the surfaces NationalCo is vacating, which caps the realized benefit. Contingency sunset extinguishes the fee-splitting flag and converts the book to 3-year contracted SaaS, but conversion churn cost logos and the 150-logo target was missed a third time. ARR quality up, take-rate down by design.

resolutions.move: Defensible-Automation enterprise expansion to the carrier tier
resolutions.rationale: GovProgramCo deepened usage as its re-tightening scaled; RegionalMutual bought a narrow governance layer above its incumbent stack; NationalCo built internally, as its $1.5B-scale AI program made probable. Revenue lands late in the window with material contracted backlog at exit — real, but partially recognized under the 12-24mo deployment lag.

resolutions.move: Auditable-AI model standards lobbying pivot
resolutions.rationale: W2 statute physics: enactment-to-operationalization runs 3-7 years and no player-relevant legislature moved the model language this turn. Recorded as a filed lobbying artifact with narrative value in the compliance entity's sale process; scored as an immature milestone with partial credit only, exactly as the move sheet pre-accepted.

turns.bluePosture: SHRINK THE CONTESTED SURFACE, WIN THE RESIDUAL ON ORIGINATION DATA. Blue does not out-escalate NationalCo's fee engine on volume where the capability gap is 3+; that contest is lost on D2 arithmetic. Instead Blue plays the two channels D2 actually rewards: (1) capability leapfrog where Blue holds a structural data advantage Red cannot buy — documentation origination — by industrializing Meridian's packet-at-origination layer (live since T2, maturing on the 12-24mo clock this turn) across Lakeview and Summit; and (2) dispute removal, expanding the Prairie wraparound and Summit direct contracts so that the volume Red's engine feeds on simply exits the adjudication contest. Lakeview's 2029 renewal is the turn's leverage event: for the first time it negotiates with a documented alternative (RegionalMutual's own Green-rider signature and audit exposure) rather than a naked 45% concentration. BDIX pivots from degraded forward prediction to what it is now demonstrably good at — audit-grade retrospective evidence that prices renewals, feeds Green's clawback machinery, and quietly raises Red's cumulative litigation-shock probability without Blue paying an escalation run-rate. Final-turn discipline: only assets already deployed or contracted can mature by end-2030; every move below extends something with T1/T2 paper behind it. Target scoring: leakage decline moderate coalition-wide (large on packet-defended and dispute-removed volume), adverse-action cost share down while dispute volume stays elevated, margins improve-or-hold at Meridian, Prairie, Summit; Lakeview holds.
